note: recommendation=delete items were removed in commit 0f85d2c41 (29 incl. MAX_HANDOFF_CHARS); adaptive items are open follow-ups; keep_load_bearing items were judged loop-stoppers or harmless.

findings.what_it_does: Default idle-watchdog WARNING stage: logs a soft-idle diagnostic after 10 minutes of stream silence (env ARGUS_SKILL_RUNNER_SOFT_IDLE_SECONDS).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Diagnostic emit only; nothing killed.
findings.rationale: Observability threshold; kills nothing.

findings.what_it_does: Default STALLED stage: emits stall diagnostics (process tree, tails) after 30 minutes of stream silence.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Diagnostics captured for the operator; the turn continues.
findings.rationale: Diagnostic-only stage; correct non-killing polarity.

findings.what_it_does: Default TERMINATE stage of the idle watchdog; 0 disables killing on idleness.
findings.consequence_when_hit: With the default, no turn is ever terminated for being idle; enabling is opt-in via env.
findings.rationale: The kill stage ships disabled — matching the philosophy that idle wall-clocks must not kill legitimate quiet work (long local computation, GPU waits).

findings.what_it_does: Interrupt provider that fires after 3 consecutive identical tool-call signatures on the claude backend; the watchdog then terminates the provider process to break the livelock.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The turn is killed. Legitimate identical polling — repeatedly running the same job-status command while a GPU job runs — is indistinguishable from a livelock and gets terminated.
findings.rationale: A livelock breaker is load-bearing in kind, but 3 identical calls is aggressively low. Require identical call AND identical result over a larger streak, or exempt known polling idioms, so healthy wait-and-check loops survive.

findings.what_it_does: For the dsh backend, forces all caller-passed idle-watchdog thresholds to 0 (lines 463-476) because dsh emits no stream events until its final text; only explicit ARGUS_SKILL_RUNNER_*_IDLE_SECONDS env re-enables them.
findings.consequence_when_hit: dsh turns are never idle-diagnosed or idle-killed by default, avoiding false kills of healthy silent turns.
findings.rationale: Deliberate policy literal that disables a watchdog whose input signal does not exist for this backend — the safe direction.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the error string embedded in a finalize event row.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Long errors cut in the event stream; full text remains in the raw I/O log.
findings.rationale: Event-row size bound with the full source preserved elsewhere.

findings.what_it_does: Ring-rotates the raw agent_io.jsonl transcript at 128 MiB, keeping 2 generations (env-overridable; write batching at lines 51-52).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The oldest transcript generation is deleted past ~256 MiB retained; sessions were measured at 6.1 GiB and 33 GiB before the cap existed.
findings.rationale: Unbounded raw transcripts demonstrably filled disks; the cap trades ancient debug history for survival and is env-tunable.

findings.what_it_does: Throttles copilot per-token delta progress emissions: a buffered delta is re-emitted only after 0.5s OR 256 accumulated chars (env ARGUS_SKILL_STREAM_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_S).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Intermediate cockpit updates are suppressed inside the window; the final message always emits and the raw stream is fully retained in the outbox.
findings.rationale: Prevents one-event-per-token spam into the sink; lossless because it only gates transient replace-in-place rows.

findings.what_it_does: Character-growth companion to the delta throttle above (env ARGUS_SKILL_STREAM_PROGRESS_CHARS).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A fast-growing delta can bypass the 0.5s interval once 256 new chars accumulate.
findings.rationale: Same lossless throttle; the pair balances latency against event volume and both are env-tunable.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the in-RAM capture deques and the stream queue for a provider turn (lines 16-19; all env-overridable).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Oldest lines/events are evicted from the in-memory result object; the complete provider output is persisted in the agent I/O logs.
findings.rationale: Bounds RAM for arbitrarily chatty providers while the full transcript survives on disk — nothing is truly lost.

findings.what_it_does: Default per-role turn wall-clock limits (lines 21/23/25); 0 disables. When set, the provider is terminated with 'wall-clock limit reached... yield for review/steering'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: With defaults, turns are never wall-clock killed; if an operator enables a limit, the turn is terminated at it.
findings.rationale: The work-killing mechanism ships disabled and opt-in — the correct default per the operator philosophy.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the `opencode db path` metadata subprocess during database recovery (sqlite connect timeout 5.0 at line 221).
findings.consequence_when_hit: TimeoutExpired makes the recovery attempt fail and the turn is reported failed.
findings.rationale: A tiny metadata command; 10s is generous, and an opencode binary that cannot print its db path in 10s will not recover the database either.

findings.symbol: kill-escalation graces (SIGTERM wait / group wait / post-SIGKILL wait / Windows wait)
findings.what_it_does: Grace periods in the termination escalation ladder (lines 154, 160, 170, 182, 190) applied after termination has already been decided.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A process ignoring SIGTERM is SIGKILLed after the grace; waits bound the reap.
findings.rationale: These do not decide to kill — they bound cleanup after a kill decision made elsewhere.

findings.what_it_does: Refuses to pass a claude prompt larger than the platform-safe argv limit, raising RuntimeError.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The turn fails fast with a clear message instead of an opaque OS exec failure.
findings.rationale: Encodes real OS argv limits; failing fast is correct, though a file-spill fallback like dsh's would be even better.

findings.what_it_does: Oversized dsh prompts are written to a file with a small argv directive pointing at it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Graceful degradation; no data loss and no failure.
findings.rationale: OS argv constraint handled with a lossless fallback — the model pattern for the claude cap above.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds how long output is still retained from pipes held open by grandchildren after the provider exits; already-queued lines are consumed.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Output written by orphans more than 5s after provider exit is no longer retained in this turn's captures.
findings.rationale: Without the bound, a grandchild holding the pipe open would hang the turn indefinitely; the turn is already over and its result complete.

findings.what_it_does: After the provider exits, waits 0.5s for legitimately-launched durable children to setsid() out of the provider's process group before the group is swept with SIGTERM.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Under scheduler pressure a legitimate durable child (e.g. a just-launched GPU job) that has not yet executed setsid is classified as a leaked orphan and SIGTERMed — silently killing intended long-running work.
findings.rationale: The 0.5s window races the OS scheduler. Re-scan group membership over a few short intervals and only sweep members that persist, or verify the child's start command against tracked external work, instead of one fixed grace.

findings.what_it_does: Final wait for provider exit after both stdout/stderr pipes have closed.
findings.consequence_when_hit: TimeoutExpired is not caught at this site: a provider lingering more than 10s after closing its pipes raises out of the stream loop, discarding the fully collected turn state instead of finalizing it.
findings.rationale: Some bound is needed (a provider can linger arbitrarily after closing pipes), and pipes-closed means output is complete — but the timeout should be caught so the collected state is salvaged and kill-escalation invoked rather than erroring the whole turn.

findings.what_it_does: Default idle caps for ACP prompt turns; 0 disables them.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A live role turn may think indefinitely without being idle-killed, by design.
findings.rationale: Work-killing off by default; enabling is an explicit operator choice.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the gap between sending ACP session/cancel and forcing the prompt loop to break.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A cancel the server never acknowledges is forced through after 5s — cancellation was already decided.
findings.rationale: Post-decision escalation bound preventing a hung cancel from wedging the client.

findings.what_it_does: The warm Manager front-door ACP session is discarded and recreated every 12 prompt calls (env ARGUS_SKILL_COPILOT_ACP_SESSION_RECYCLE).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The 12th call pays session re-setup latency and loses in-session context; bounds unbounded resume-cost growth.
findings.rationale: The right trigger is measured context size or per-call latency/cost climbing past a threshold, not a fixed call count; 12 is a pure judgment call, though env-overridable.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the ACP initialize/authenticate handshake when starting the copilot --acp subprocess; RuntimeError on expiry.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The warm client fails to start and the turn falls back/fails before any model spend.
findings.rationale: Transport handshake, not model thinking time; a handshake that has produced nothing in 30s is genuinely wedged.

findings.what_it_does: Grace after terminate() (line 365) and after kill() (line 369) when closing a warm ACP client.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A subprocess ignoring terminate is killed 2s later — shutdown already decided.
findings.rationale: Post-decision cleanup escalation.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the session/new (line 668) and session/load (line 701) JSON-RPC calls; RuntimeError on expiry.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Turn setup fails cleanly before the prompt is sent; no partial model work is lost.
findings.rationale: Session setup is protocol traffic with no legitimate long-thinking phase.

findings.what_it_does: Derives the ACP idle-watchdog poll cadence from the configured thresholds, clamped to 0.01-0.25s.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Watchdog wakes at most every 0.25s; already scales with the thresholds it enforces.
findings.rationale: This is the adaptive pattern done right — the literals are only clamps.

findings.what_it_does: LRU cap on warm ACP clients kept per scope; the least-recently-used client is closed on overflow.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The evicted label pays a cold ACP start on its next call; the running turn is unaffected.
findings.rationale: Bounds resident copilot subprocesses; eviction costs latency, not work.

findings.what_it_does: Prunes Argus-owned copilot session scratch older than 7 days (env ARGUS_SKILL_COPILOT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS; 0 disables). Growth measured at 2.6 GB/day unpruned.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Session state older than 7 days is deleted; a thread resumed after more than 7 idle days loses its session store.
findings.rationale: Disk-growth fence with an env override and a disable escape hatch; 7 days comfortably exceeds realistic resume gaps.

findings.what_it_does: Throttles the retention sweep to once per hour via a stamp file.
findings.consequence_when_hit: At most one directory sweep per hour regardless of call volume.
findings.rationale: IO throttle on a janitorial task.

findings.what_it_does: Runner-wide soft idle threshold for all role backends: after 10 minutes without backend events the watchdog raises a soft-idle signal (status/nudge).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Status/inactivity reporting only at this tier; the run continues.
findings.rationale: Soft tier only observes and reports; some threshold must exist to distinguish 'quiet' from 'normal', and its consequence is harmless. Env-overridable for unusual workloads.

findings.what_it_does: Runner-wide stalled-idle threshold: 30 minutes of backend silence marks the role session stalled (hard-kill tier is separately 0/disabled by default at line 210).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The session is flagged stalled and stall-handling kicks in, even if a legitimate long GPU/compile step is simply quiet on the event stream.
findings.rationale: For a daemon that launches multi-hour GPU training, 30 minutes of event silence is common while a foreground training script runs. Stalledness should be judged by process/GPU liveness (child process alive, GPU utilization, log file mtime) rather than event-stream silence; note the hard-kill tier correctly defaults to 0 (disabled), which is the right pattern.

findings.what_it_does: Fixed pacing of the life supervisor's main loop (mission pickup, inbox drain, stop-event checks). Unlike the daemon poll (ARGUS_SKILL_DAEMON_POLL_S, default 5.0 at apps/cli/_core.py:702), this one has no override.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Up to 2s latency on reacting to new work or a stop request; negligible CPU cost.
findings.rationale: A short fixed poll on a long-lived supervisor is benign pacing, not policy: it kills nothing, drops nothing, and 2s reaction latency is invisible against hours-long missions. Only inconsistency with the env-tunable sibling is worth noting.

findings.what_it_does: Runs the SELF-profile learning review only after 5 new operator turns since the last review (over the last 12 turns).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Below the threshold, no self-learning review runs; potential lessons from recent chats wait.
findings.rationale: A fixed 5-turn cadence is a judgment call about when enough new material exists; the trigger could instead be content-driven (e.g. review when idle, or when the accumulated un-reviewed turns exceed a token budget) — though the cost of the current value is low.

findings.what_it_does: Hard idle watchdog for the Manager SELF-reply session: 120s with no backend event aborts the run (soft-idle status at 5s, line 820).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The SELF turn is killed mid-flight; the operator's chat message gets an error path instead of an answer.
findings.rationale: Idle-based (liveness-style) rather than wall-clock, which is right, but 120s is tight for a SELF turn that legitimately runs a slow shell command or a long reasoning stretch with buffered output. Should scale with the execution contract chosen for the turn (micro vs implement) or at minimum match the runner-wide idle defaults.

findings.what_it_does: If the SELF call fails on a known transport error (ACP died, network_error, endpoint unavailable), retries exactly once in a fresh session; both attempts' tokens are accounted.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Second failure surfaces to the operator; no further retries.
findings.rationale: Bounded single retry over an enumerated transient-error allowlist recovers the common blip without any possibility of a retry loop; unbounded retry here would silently burn calls against a dead endpoint.

findings.what_it_does: Default number of concurrent path-disjoint mission workers the daemon runs (0 pauses, 1 serial, N parallel); documented in --help and overridable per launch.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Out of the box, at most 2 missions run concurrently regardless of machine capacity or how parallelizable the planner's task graph is.
findings.rationale: Width is a capacity judgment: on the operator's 4×A6000 box with disjoint tasks, 2 leaves hardware idle; on a laptop it may thrash. A default derived from available resources (GPU count, provider concurrency budget) fits the philosophy better than a fixed 2 — mitigated by being a visible, documented CLI default rather than a buried constant.

findings.what_it_does: Sets stream-idle watchdog tiers for the one-shot read-only readiness probe: warn at 15s, alert at 45s, kill the provider process group at 90s of no output.
findings.consequence_when_hit: At 90s idle the probe's provider process is killed and setup/readiness verification reports the backend as not ready. A slow-but-healthy backend (e.g. a reasoning model with long time-to-first-token) can false-fail setup.
findings.rationale: The code comment is honest ('bounds a one-shot readiness probe, not a production role turn') and some bound is needed so a wedged CLI cannot hang setup forever, but 90s is a guess about provider latency. Deriving the hard tier from observed backend first-token latency (or retrying once with a longer bound) would remove false 'not ready' verdicts without unbounding the probe.

findings.what_it_does: Watchdog tiers for the doctor's agent-driven repair turn: warn at 30s idle, alert at 120s, hard kill disabled (0).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Soft/stalled tiers only emit diagnostics; nothing is ever killed because hard idle is 0.
findings.rationale: Exactly the right shape under the operator philosophy: the repair turn is never killed by wall clock, and the 30/120 numbers only control when warnings appear. Harmless diagnostic thresholds.

findings.what_it_does: Subprocess timeout for backend CLI readiness probes (--version, model listing, auth checks) via _run_text; default parameter of check_backend_readiness (line 750).
findings.consequence_when_hit: TimeoutExpired is caught and reported as a readiness problem — the doctor says the backend is not ready. No running work is affected; only diagnostics.
findings.rationale: Bounds a diagnostic probe, not production work; a CLI that cannot print its version in 30s is genuinely broken, and without the bound a wedged CLI would hang doctor/setup forever. The version check even gets one retry on timeout (line 799).

findings.symbol: Copilot ACP auth probe retry loop
findings.what_it_does: Retries the Copilot ACP auth probe exactly once when the first attempt fails with 'acp initialize failed:'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: After the second failure the backend is reported not ready.
findings.rationale: A minimal, bounded retry that absorbs one-off ACP startup flakiness in a diagnostic path. More retries would only slow doctor runs against a genuinely broken backend.

findings.what_it_does: Retries the backend CLI --version probe once if the first invocation times out (lines 807-809).
findings.consequence_when_hit: After the second timeout the backend is reported not ready.
findings.rationale: Bounded flake absorption in a readiness diagnostic; keeps the doctor honest without looping forever on a dead CLI.

findings.symbol: _CALL_STATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (with 10ms poll at line 190 and 0.25 defaults at lines 354/548/602)
findings.what_it_does: Bounds how long cost-control call-state lock acquisition waits before raising CostControlLockBusyError; used by reserve_call_budget's telemetry write and cost_control_snapshot.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Deliberate graceful degradation, verified in code: in reserve_call_budget (lines 434-439) only the telemetry reservation record is skipped (state_tracked=False) — the authoritative settled-spend admission check already passed; in metrics snapshotting the busy error is treated as transient and the snapshot is retried later. No work is denied or killed.
findings.rationale: The short bound prevents lock convoys on the hot per-call path, and every busy outcome degrades to a benign skipped telemetry write rather than a spend-policy error. The mechanism is doing exactly what a non-blocking fast path should.

findings.what_it_does: Maximum time exclusive_file_lock will contend for an advisory portalocker/fcntl file lock before giving up.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Raises TimeoutError('timed out acquiring {name} after 30s') at line 34 — the caller's state operation fails loudly instead of hanging. Since OS advisory locks die with their holder, a timeout means a live holder held the lock 30s, so a genuinely slow (not crashed) state operation aborts a concurrent legitimate one.
findings.rationale: Bounded lock acquisition is what turns a wedged holder into a diagnosable error at the state boundary rather than a silent fleet-wide hang. State-file critical sections are all small writes, so 30s is far above any legitimate hold time; the failure mode is loud and retryable by the caller.

findings.what_it_does: Sleep interval between non-blocking lock acquisition attempts inside exclusive_file_lock.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Adds up to 50ms latency per contention cycle; negligible CPU cost.
findings.rationale: Plain poll-interval plumbing with no policy content; 50ms is a reasonable balance between latency and spin, and there is nothing to derive it from.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback for the host-global daily spend cap used by cost-control admission when neither env nor persisted config sets it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: reserve_call_budget denies new provider calls with stop_kind='budget_exhausted'; all daemons on the host pause spending until the day rolls over.
findings.rationale: A spend circuit breaker is exactly the load-bearing class of limit; the default is set high enough ($20k/day) to act as a catastrophic-runaway backstop rather than a routine throttle, and the knob registry gives env and persisted override. Deleting the fallback would leave runaway spend unbounded.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback cap on concurrently active Argus daemons per host (env/persisted overridable); the adjacent comment notes daemon count is decoupled from provider concurrency.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Launching daemon number 65 is refused — a host-resource admission decision, not a kill of running work.
findings.rationale: A hard ceiling on daemon fan-out is a resource/LLM-burn safety cap; 64 is generous enough that hitting it signals a runaway launcher rather than legitimate demand, and the refusal is at admission time with a clear override path.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback minimum interval between Curator strategy-distillation LLM runs.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A Curator update opportunity inside the cooldown is skipped; strategy digest refreshes at most every 21 minutes.
findings.rationale: This cooldown is a rate limiter on recurring LLM calls — the burn-prevention class the operator treats as load-bearing. The precise value (21 min) is a judgment call but low-stakes: it delays a periodic distillation, never blocks or kills mission work, and is env/persisted tunable.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback 'hard safety ceiling' caps on team fan-out: teammates per team, concurrent campaigns, tasks per formation, and total in-flight teammate turns.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Spawn/launch requests beyond the cap are refused at admission; existing work continues.
findings.rationale: These are exactly the loop-stopper/fan-out circuit breakers that prevent a planner bug from spawning unbounded LLM-consuming teammates. Values are arbitrary but deliberately generous, refusal happens before work starts, and all are overridable knobs.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback quotas for the Copilot provider guard: daily premium requests, daily calls, hourly calls, and concurrent calls.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Permit denied with stop_kind='budget_exhausted'; Copilot-backed work pauses until the window resets.
findings.rationale: Same circuit-breaker family as the Codex cap; the 10000 defaults are effectively 'off unless something is very wrong', which is the right default posture for a backstop. Real quota tuning happens via the env/persisted knob.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback for how many consecutive same-family subagent failures the L4 planner tolerates before circuit-breaking further retries of that experiment family.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The planner stops re-launching that family — a research direction is abandoned/escalated after 3 consecutive failures inside the window.
findings.rationale: This is a loop-stopper against burning GPU-hours and LLM calls re-running a doomed approach, squarely in the load-bearing class. 3 is a judgment call, but it gates retries of an already-failing family (each failure may represent hours of work), and the knob is overridable for campaigns where persistence is warranted.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback trailing window within which same-family failures count toward the streak limit; failures older than 72h age out.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A slow-failing family (e.g. multi-day GPU jobs) may never accumulate a streak, or a fast-failing one trips quickly; the window shape decides which failures 'count'.
findings.rationale: Unlike the streak count, the window duration should track observed job duration: 72h is 3+ streak-triggering failures for hour-long jobs but can be under one attempt for multi-day training runs, silently disabling the circuit breaker exactly where failures are most expensive. Deriving the window from the family's own attempt durations (e.g. N times median runtime) would make the streak semantics uniform.

findings.symbol: ARGUS_SKILL_RUNNER_SOFT_IDLE_SECONDS / RUNNER_STALLED_IDLE_SECONDS defaults (lines 163-164; HARD_IDLE default 0 at line 165)
findings.what_it_does: Fallback production-runner watchdog tiers: diagnostic warning after 10 min of provider-stream silence, stalled alert after 30 min; the kill tier defaults to disabled.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Log warning and operator alert respectively — no process is ever killed by default because hard idle is 0.
findings.rationale: The dangerous tier (kill) is off by default, honoring the no-wall-clock-kills philosophy; 600/1800 only control alert noise. Reasonable diagnostic defaults with env/persisted override for chatty or quiet backends.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback count of hot (uncompressed) history/wiki versions kept before older versions are gzip-compressed.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Versions beyond the 20 newest are compressed losslessly — access gets slightly slower, nothing is dropped.
findings.rationale: Lossless housekeeping: the number only trades disk for read latency, with no data loss and a knob override. No policy judgment is being smuggled in.

findings.what_it_does: Env-overridable fallbacks for metrics.jsonl rotation (at 16MiB) and archive pruning (delete archives older than 7 days or beyond the 14 newest) in _rotate_if_needed/_prune_archives.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Telemetry archives are permanently unlinked once they age past 7 days or exceed 14 files — historical metrics are lost; the live file is rotated, never task execution touched (the header comment says exactly this).
findings.rationale: Unbounded telemetry growth on a 7x24 host is a real disk-exhaustion risk, and only observability data (never scientific artifacts or events.jsonl) is discarded. The retention numbers encode mild judgment but are env-tunable and the failure mode is losing old graphs, not work.

findings.value: provider: attempts>=5 and success<0.95; command: attempts>=3 and success<0.98; web 5xx rate > 0.01
findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded minimum-sample gates and success-rate/error-rate thresholds that decide when an SLO violation string is appended to the SLO report.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A violation line appears in the SLO report — alerting/observability only; no work is gated, paused, or killed.
findings.rationale: These five numbers (5, 0.95, 3, 0.98, 0.01) are pure judgment calls about what 'unhealthy' means, buried in code rather than the knob registry, so an operator cannot tune alert sensitivity without a code change. Consequence is only report noise, so no urgency — but they belong in the knob registry or derived from trailing baselines rather than hardcoded.

findings.symbol: _text default char limit (and per-call caps of 160/180/240/500/1000/2000/4000 across reducers)
findings.what_it_does: Default character cap on any event text pulled into the mission view; individual reducer call sites choose tighter or looser caps (e.g. title[:180]/detail[:500] at lines 104-105, title[:240]/detail[:4000] at 144-145).
findings.consequence_when_hit: View text is silently clipped; full text remains in events.jsonl.
findings.rationale: Presentation-layer clipping inside a deliberately bounded projection. The scatter of per-site magic caps (160/240/4000...) is untidy but each is a display judgment with no effect on the record of truth.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the mission-view timeline at the newest 120 rows (rows[-120:] in _reduce_helpers.py:113).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older timeline entries silently disappear from the cockpit UI; the full record survives in events.jsonl, from which the view is rebuildable.
findings.rationale: The view is an intentionally bounded projection, not the record of truth — nothing is lost, only elided from a UI JSON that must stay small enough to write atomically on every event. The specific 120 is arbitrary but low-stakes.

findings.what_it_does: Caps per-role work-history entries retained in the mission view (applied in _reduce_helpers.py:160).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older per-role work items drop out of the cockpit view; recoverable from events.jsonl.
findings.rationale: Same bounded-projection argument as the timeline cap: UI state must stay bounded, the event log remains complete.

findings.what_it_does: When rebuilding the mission view from scratch, _tail_jsonl (lines 277-301) reads only the last 8 MiB of events.jsonl.
findings.consequence_when_hit: For a long campaign whose event log exceeds 8 MiB, everything earlier is silently excluded from the rebuilt view — cumulative fields reduced from events (counters, role histories, early milestones) can be permanently wrong in the cockpit after a rebuild, with no truncation flag.
findings.rationale: This is the one mission-view cap where truncation is both silent and potentially semantic: a rebuild is supposed to reproduce the view, and the tail-read quietly changes reduction results once the log outgrows 8 MiB — exactly on the long campaigns Argus is built for. Streaming the whole file (reduction is line-at-a-time; memory need not scale with file size), or at minimum stamping the rebuilt view with a bootstrap_truncated flag, would remove the silent divergence.

findings.what_it_does: Caps skill-document content embedded in the mission-view snapshot; _snapshot.py lines 368-377 truncate and set skill['content_truncated'] = True.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Skill text beyond 128 KiB is cut from the view payload, with an explicit truncation flag so the UI can say so.
findings.rationale: Flagged (not silent) truncation of display payload in a bounded UI projection; the source document is untouched on disk.

findings.symbol: operator decision option cap (label[:160] at line 33, description[:1000] at line 51)
findings.what_it_does: Normalizing an operator decision request keeps at most 8 options (silently dropping extras), with labels clipped to 160 chars and descriptions to 1000.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If an agent proposes more than 8 choices for the operator, options 9+ never reach the human — a path the agent recommended can be silently removed from the ballot.
findings.rationale: A decision surface with dozens of options is a malformed request, and the cap defends the operator UI from a runaway LLM reply; 8 is a sane ballot size. The silent drop is the only blemish — logging when options are discarded would make it clean — but the bound itself is protective.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback price per Copilot premium request used in budget accounting when ARGUS_SKILL_COPILOT_USD_PER_PREMIUM_REQUEST is unset, invalid, or negative.
findings.consequence_when_hit: All Copilot premium-request spend is valued at $0.04 each; if GitHub's real rate diverges, settled-cost admission and daily-cap math drift accordingly (over- or under-throttling).
findings.rationale: It mirrors GitHub's published $0.04/premium-request rate — closer to a provider pricing fact (like the per-token tables) than a judgment call — and a zero fallback would make premium spend invisible to the budget breaker, which is strictly worse. Env override is the correction path when the vendor reprices.

findings.what_it_does: Default TTL for an operator confirmation token authorizing precise-clause contract revisions (default ttl_seconds of issue_confirmation, sets expires_at).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A revision presented with an expired confirmation is refused with ContractError; the operator must re-confirm. No running work is affected.
findings.rationale: The comment states the intent: 'Confirmation expiry bounds stale operator authority, not execution time.' Bounding replay of week-old authority over contract changes is a security/consistency property; 7 days is a defensible staleness bar and the parameter is caller-overridable.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback (env ARGUS_SKILL_PROJECT_RETENTION_DAYS overrides via retention_days_default) for how long a non-live project directory may sit untouched before GC moves it to projects_trash/<date>/.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A project parked >30 days with no live daemon is moved (never rm'd) into a dated trash directory; recovery is a move back. Live daemons are never touched, and negative retention raises ValueError.
findings.rationale: The operation is reversible by construction (move-to-trash, no deletion) and live-daemon-protected, so the worst false positive is an operator retrieving a directory from trash. Some default must exist for housekeeping to run at all, and the env override is the tuning path.

findings.what_it_does: Grace period protecting freshly created empty project state from the GC sweep; the comment states 'it never bounds work'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An empty project directory older than 1 hour with no live daemon is swept to trash; younger ones are left alone.
findings.rationale: A protective window (it prevents GC racing project creation), reversible outcome, explicit design comment. One hour comfortably exceeds any legitimate gap between mkdir and first state write.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback for the host-global Codex daily call cap when ARGUS_SKILL_CODEX_DAILY_CALL_CAP is not set (env or persisted config); enforced at line 174.
findings.consequence_when_hit: acquire_codex_permit denies with reason 'global Codex daily call cap 300 reached' and stop_kind='budget_exhausted' — all Codex-backed missions on the host pause until the next local day.
findings.rationale: This is the canonical LLM-burn circuit breaker the operator philosophy explicitly blesses, and it degrades to a clean pause rather than killed work. The specific value 300 is a judgment call worth operator review (a heavy legitimate campaign can hit it and stall for hours), but the mechanism and a hardcoded fallback must exist — env/persisted override is already the tuning path.

findings.what_it_does: Normalizes a reviewer's research result by keeping at most 12 evidence entries and 12 limitations, each clipped to 500 characters, silently discarding the rest.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Evidence items beyond the 12th vanish from the normalized record that downstream completion checks and the certified result are built on — the scientific record of what supports a claimed result is silently thinned.
findings.rationale: Evidence lists are the load-bearing scientific artifact here, and research_completion_issue gates on result['evidence'] being non-empty — the caps affect certified content, not display. A rich result with 20 evidence pointers loses 8 with no flag. The bound should be generous and overflow should be flagged or spilled to the evidence ledger, not discarded; 12/500 encodes an unstated judgment about how much evidence a result may have.

findings.symbol: repository map entry cap (and checkpoint open-items cap at line 130)
findings.what_it_does: The prompt-context repository listing is capped at 80 sorted directory entries, and the checkpoint's 'Open Questions / Blockers' carried into the next turn is capped at 20 items — both silently.
findings.consequence_when_hit: In a large workdir, files past the 80th sorted entry never appear in the role's map (sorted order means late-alphabet files are systematically invisible); open questions beyond 20 are dropped from the handoff.
findings.rationale: Both caps ration prompt space, so the honest bound is token-budget-derived per model rather than fixed counts; the sorted-prefix repository listing additionally has a systematic bias (alphabetical survivorship) that a smarter selection (recently modified, or role-relevant) would fix. Silent loss of open questions is planner-memory decay, same family as the frontier caps.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates decisive output and detail strings persisted into the role-session capsule that seeds subsequent turns.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Tail of long decisive outputs is silently cut from cross-turn memory; the full text exists only in the transcript.
findings.rationale: Same context-rationing family as the frontier text caps: fixed character counts stand in for a token budget the system already knows per model. Low urgency (transcript retains the full text) but the truncation is silent where a marker or summary would be nearly free.

findings.what_it_does: Poll interval while waiting (unboundedly) for a free cross-process role concurrency slot; slot counts come from env ARGUS_SKILL_<ROLE>_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 0 = unlimited).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The waiter checks for a slot ten times a second and never abandons the wait — work queues instead of being killed.
findings.rationale: The unbounded wait is the philosophically correct part (no work abandoned by wall clock); the 100ms poll is mechanical plumbing with negligible cost. Nothing to derive.

findings.symbol: git subprocess timeouts (rev-parse / symbolic-ref / status --porcelain, lines 38, 52, 56)
findings.what_it_does: Bounds the git subprocess calls used to stamp runtime identity (revision, branch, dirty flag) into diagnostics.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Exception is caught; identity fields degrade to revision=None / git_available=False. Nothing is killed — telemetry is just less informative.
findings.rationale: Fail-fast on a purely diagnostic lookup. On a very large repo `git status --porcelain` can exceed 2s and habitually blank the dirty flag, which is the only mild cost; the degradation is cosmetic and the bound keeps identity capture off the critical path.

findings.what_it_does: Files larger than 32 MiB are skipped by the secret scrub (lines 595-601); text/source-suffixed skips set report.truncated = True.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Secrets embedded in a >32 MiB text artifact are NOT redacted before the artifact is shared/published — a security-coverage gap, though the report flags that the scan was truncated.
findings.rationale: The cap exists because the file is read wholly into memory; scanning in streamed chunks (with overlap for boundary-straddling matches) removes the need for any size cap on the security-critical path. Until then the flag prevents silent failure, but a hardcoded ceiling on secret-scan coverage is the wrong place to economize.

findings.what_it_does: The artifact secret scan stops after 10,000 files (check at 575-577, break at 652-653) and marks the report truncated.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Files beyond the first 10k are never scanned for secrets; the truncated flag surfaces the gap but does not close it.
findings.rationale: Bounds scrub time against a pathological tree (e.g. a node_modules or dataset directory swept into artifacts); the scan already prioritizes git-changed paths, hitting 10k files signals a mis-scoped artifact set rather than legitimate need, and the truncation is flagged. Raising it costs linear scan time with fast-diminishing coverage value.

findings.what_it_does: Caps list fields (resolved/new obligations, evidence refs, etc.) taken from a single reviewer-authored frontier transition.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Items beyond 40 in one transition are silently dropped before ever entering frontier state.
findings.rationale: A single review turn legitimately producing >40 distinct obligations indicates a malformed or runaway reply; the cap defends state size against one bad LLM output. Contrast with the cumulative _merge cap below, which is the one that loses real history.

findings.symbol: _merge cumulative list cap (also per-field limit=80 in from_dict, lines 140-145)
findings.what_it_does: When merging each transition into cumulative frontier state (open obligations, evidence, etc.), keeps only the most recent 80 items per field.
findings.consequence_when_hit: On a long campaign the oldest unresolved obligations and evidence references are silently forgotten — planner-visible research memory decays with no flag and no recovery path in the frontier itself.
findings.rationale: This cap erodes exactly the state Argus's months-long campaigns depend on: an obligation dropped at item 81 is an open commitment the planner will never see again, and the loss is silent. The bound should derive from what the consuming prompt can carry (token budget of the planner context), with overflow spilled to a durable side ledger or summarized rather than discarded.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates reviewer-authored frontier text: regression-envelope fields, hypothesis, uncertainty, decision, and summary strings.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Text beyond the cap is silently cut from planner-visible memory — a long hypothesis or uncertainty statement loses its tail with no marker.
findings.rationale: These fields are the model's working memory across turns, so the right bound is a function of the consuming model's context budget, not a fixed 1000/2000. Silent truncation of mid-sentence reasoning is worse than either a visible '[truncated]' marker or a summarize-on-overflow step.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the stored frontier transition history at the most recent 100 records.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Transitions older than the last 100 are silently dropped from frontier state; early-campaign reasoning history becomes unreachable through the frontier.
findings.rationale: Same silent-memory-decay pattern as the _merge cap, milder because history is more audit trail than active planning input; long campaigns exceed 100 transitions. Deriving from consumer needs, or archiving evicted records instead of discarding, fits the system's otherwise lossless posture (events.jsonl, gzip history).

findings.what_it_does: After 2 consecutive failures with no change in the failure signature, the frontier's disposition flips to 'diagnose_or_replan', steering the planner away from re-running the same approach.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The planner is directed to diagnose or replan instead of retrying — no work is killed; the third identical attempt is discouraged, not forbidden.
findings.rationale: This is the loop-stopper against burning GPU-hours repeating an unchanged failure — the class the operator explicitly protects. 2 is aggressive but the consequence is advisory (a disposition string the planner reads), making it cheap when wrong and valuable when right.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the in-memory call-id deduplication cache; on overflow (lines 738-744) the oldest entry/project is evicted.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Dedup falls back to re-reading usage records from disk — a pure performance cost; correctness of dedup is preserved.
findings.rationale: Classic bounded-memory cache in a long-lived daemon; eviction degrades to slower disk reads, never wrong accounting. Nothing to derive.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the error string stored in a usage record to 2000 characters.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Tail of a very long provider error message is silently dropped from the usage ledger.
findings.rationale: Keeps a per-call ledger line bounded; 2000 chars preserves any actionable error prefix, and the full error surfaces through the runner's own logs. Minor, silent, but low-stakes.

findings.what_it_does: Network timeout per provider-route liveness probe (a minimal completion request) during vault preflight before 7x24 daemon boot.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The route is marked not alive; if it is a required route, preflight fails and the daemon refuses to start. A loaded-but-healthy endpoint that takes >10s to answer a 16-token completion false-fails boot.
findings.rationale: This is a wall-clock timeout whose false positive blocks legitimate work (daemon start) — the worst-offender class under the operator philosophy. Preflight runs once at boot where seconds are cheap: retrying with escalating timeouts (10s, 30s, 60s) before declaring a route dead would eliminate false boot failures while still catching black-holed endpoints.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the clean-launch probe subprocess run before a mission executor spawn is admitted.
findings.consequence_when_hit: TimeoutExpired is treated as a failed spawn (rc 2); the mission does not start.
findings.rationale: On a loaded box (cold FS cache, Python import storms) a healthy interpreter launch can exceed 15s, turning machine load into spurious spawn failures. Scale with observed launch latency or check that the probe process is alive and making progress instead of a fixed wall clock.

findings.what_it_does: Extra margin added to the clean-launch probe timeout on Windows.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Same as the base timeout: probe declared failed, spawn aborted, at 30s total on Windows.
findings.rationale: Same wall-clock-versus-load problem as the base constant; the fixed +15s acknowledges Windows is slower but still encodes a guess.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the spawn-failure error text captured into daemon state.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Error text beyond 8000 chars is silently truncated in the receipt; full output remains in the spawn log file.
findings.rationale: Bounds state-file growth; the underlying log retains the full text.

findings.what_it_does: Clock-skew margin when deciding whether a spawn log file is fresh evidence of the launch under test.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A log modified more than 2s before the spawn started is treated as stale and not used as failure evidence.
findings.rationale: Small skew tolerance for filesystem timestamp granularity; affects only which diagnostics are attributed, not whether work runs.

findings.what_it_does: Keeps only the last 4000 chars of the spawn log when reporting a failed launch.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Earlier log content omitted from the report; full file remains on disk.
findings.rationale: Diagnostic excerpt cap with the full source preserved.

findings.what_it_does: A 1s-poll watchdog thread fails every durable backlog claim in status 'running' when no supervisor call is in flight and every role-activity heartbeat has been quiet for more than 30 seconds.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The mission is marked FAILED with 'executor exited without completing the task' and a LIFE_MISSION_COMPLETED success=False event is emitted. Any in-daemon pause over 30s that is not a supervisor call — inter-round bookkeeping, large git operations, slow state writes — irrecoverably fails an otherwise healthy mission.
findings.rationale: This is a wall-clock proxy for the question 'is the executor thread still alive', which can be answered directly with a thread/process liveness check. The _supervisor_execution_active guard narrows but does not eliminate false positives, and the consequence (mission failed, work abandoned) is the worst-offender pattern. Replace the 30s timer with executor-thread liveness.

findings.what_it_does: Poll cadence of the stalled-running watchdog thread.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Stall evaluation runs once per second.
findings.rationale: Mechanical cadence — though if the 30s stall mechanism is deleted per the finding above, this goes with it.

findings.what_it_does: Default cap on engineer/reviewer rounds per mission; the fallback 0 means unlimited rounds.
findings.consequence_when_hit: With the default, a reviewer that keeps answering 'continue' loops indefinitely; only the daily budget cap eventually fences the burn.
findings.rationale: This is the one place the codebase lacks a loop-stopper where the philosophy says one is usually load-bearing. A generous finite default, or a progress-based stopper (no diff/decision change across N rounds), would end silent infinite loops well before the budget fence.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcodes the supervisor poll interval in _build_supervisor_config, ignoring the configured cfg.poll_interval.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Operators tuning poll_interval in daemon config silently do not affect the supervisor loop.
findings.rationale: A config knob already exists for exactly this; the literal should be replaced with cfg.poll_interval so one setting governs both loops.

findings.what_it_does: Caps retained control-command receipts; oldest are silently pruned.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A client polling for a receipt older than the newest 1000 finds nothing.
findings.rationale: Bounds the state file; 1000 receipts far exceeds any realistic in-flight polling window.

findings.what_it_does: Bound on acquiring the command-file lock; raises TimeoutError after 30s.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The control command fails with a clear error instead of deadlocking on a stuck lock holder.
findings.rationale: Lock timeouts prevent indefinite hangs; 30s is generous for a small state file and the operation is retryable.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates error text stored in a command receipt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Long tracebacks are silently cut in the receipt; full detail requires the journal.
findings.rationale: Receipt-size bound; the journal retains full diagnostics.

findings.what_it_does: Circuit-breaker default: consecutive failures of one subagent family before the family is disabled (config-overridable; this is the hardcoded fallback).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The failing agent family is refused for new work until the failure window expires.
findings.rationale: Loop-stopper preventing repeated LLM burn against a broken provider or family; exactly the protective class the philosophy endorses.

findings.what_it_does: Window over which the family failure streak is counted (config-overridable fallback).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Failures older than 72h stop counting; a tripped breaker can suppress a family for up to 72h after its last failure.
findings.rationale: Companion to the breaker; long window only gates a family that is actually failing repeatedly, and config can shorten it.

findings.what_it_does: Daemon backlog poll cadence fallback (config-overridable).
findings.consequence_when_hit: New missions are picked up with up to 5s latency.
findings.rationale: Ordinary poll cadence; harmless latency versus CPU tradeoff.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback for the global daily spend cap when config omits it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Cost admission refuses further provider spawns for the day; the backlog stalls until rollover.
findings.rationale: The budget fence is the archetypal load-bearing gate against unbounded LLM burn; the specific dollar value is config-driven with this conservative fallback.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback for how many missions run concurrently when config omits mission_width.
findings.consequence_when_hit: At most 2 missions execute in parallel; backlog beyond that serializes.
findings.rationale: Fixed 2 encodes a guess about machine and provider-quota capacity; could derive from cores, quota headroom, or budget while keeping the config override.

findings.what_it_does: Default age filter for classifying a process as a foreground wait shell in the standalone listing helper (also the sleep-duration threshold: sleep N qualifies only when N >= this value).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Processes younger than 60s, or sleeps shorter than 60s, are not classified as wait shells and are left alone.
findings.rationale: The generous 60s default errs on the side of not touching processes; misclassification risk drops with age. Callers can pass a different value.

findings.what_it_does: Scan cadence of the foreground-wait guard thread (floored to 1.0 at construction).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Wait shells are detected at up to 5s latency; lower values add process-table scan overhead.
findings.rationale: Plain poll cadence with a sane floor; no work-killing behavior of its own.

findings.what_it_does: The resident guard SIGTERMs agent-owned foreground wait shells (tail --pid -f /dev/null, sleep >= threshold, python pidfd/inotify wait one-liners) at least 15s old whenever tracked external work is waitable.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A wait shell the agent deliberately started is killed roughly 15-20s in; the agent's foreground command returns killed and the turn is expected to yield. A legitimate short sleep-and-recheck loop the agent chose is terminated.
findings.rationale: The mechanism itself protects turns from blocking on local polls while durable external work runs, but 15s is a fixed judgment call barely three scan intervals long. Scale the threshold with interval_seconds and require the same wait idiom observed on consecutive scans before terminating.

findings.what_it_does: The upgraded daemon candidate must reach handoff standby within 30s or proc.terminate() is called and the handoff is aborted and rolled back.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A healthy but slow-starting candidate (cold caches, loaded box) is killed and the deployment handoff fails; the old runtime keeps running.
findings.rationale: A wall-clock gate on legitimate startup work. A liveness/progress check on the candidate (process alive and importing, standby file partially advanced) or a threshold scaled to observed startup times would avoid killing slow-but-healthy candidates. Failure mode is at least safe (rollback, incumbent survives).

findings.what_it_does: Poll cadence while waiting for the candidate standby marker (also lines 207 and 233).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Standby detected within 100ms of appearing.
findings.rationale: Mechanical local-file poll cadence.

findings.what_it_does: Bound on acquiring the daemon PID lock during handoff adoption.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Handoff exits rc 2 as DaemonAlreadyRunning; nothing is killed.
findings.rationale: Lock-acquisition bound preventing an indefinite hang; failure is a clean refusal.

findings.what_it_does: Threshold for reporting the daemon as stalled in health/status output (env ARGUS_SKILL_DAEMON_STALL_SECONDS).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Diagnostic only: the daemon is flagged stalled in status and journal; nothing is killed.
findings.rationale: Pure observability threshold with an env override; exactly how a stall detector should behave — report, never terminate.

findings.what_it_does: Throttle on activity-heartbeat file writes.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The heartbeat timestamp is up to 5s stale, bounding stall-detector granularity and disk write rate.
findings.rationale: IO-throttle for a diagnostic signal; 5s is negligible against a 1800s stall threshold.

findings.what_it_does: Retry count for os.replace on Windows sharing violations when writing the heartbeat file (with doubling backoff).
findings.consequence_when_hit: After 6 attempts (~0.6s of backoff) the heartbeat write is abandoned; the health file skips a beat.
findings.rationale: Bounded retry around a transient AV/indexer race; failure is a missed diagnostic beat, not lost work.

findings.what_it_does: Initial delay for the Windows replace retry loop, doubled each attempt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Total backoff tops out around 0.63s across 6 attempts.
findings.rationale: Standard exponential backoff base for a sub-second transient race.

findings.what_it_does: Poll cadence of the daemon control-file watcher thread.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Control commands observed within 100ms.
findings.rationale: Mechanical poll cadence for responsiveness.

findings.what_it_does: Default teammate width for team missions when the env var is unset.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Team missions spawn up to 8 concurrent teammates — a concurrency and cost policy baked into a fallback string.
findings.rationale: Eight parallel LLM-driven teammates is a large cost/capacity judgment to hardcode; derive from budget headroom, provider quota, or mission_width instead of a fixed literal.

findings.what_it_does: Curator tick cadence fallback.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Team curation decisions run at 5s granularity.
findings.rationale: Ordinary scheduler cadence, env-overridable.

findings.what_it_does: Teammate wall-clock timeout; the fallback 0 disables it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: With the default, teammates run unbounded; when an operator sets a value, teammates are stopped at that wall clock.
findings.rationale: The default deliberately keeps the work-killing mechanism off, matching the philosophy that wall-clock kills are opt-in only.

findings.what_it_does: Grace between a teammate stop request and hard kill.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A teammate that ignores a stop request for 600s is force-killed — termination was already decided.
findings.rationale: Post-decision escalation grace, not a work-killing trigger; 10 minutes is generous for cleanup.

findings.what_it_does: Minimum interval between curator skill-distillation runs (each an LLM call).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Distillation is throttled to at most one run per 21 minutes.
findings.rationale: Throttles background LLM burn; the oddly specific 1260 suggests tuning happened, and the env override exists. Could be derived from activity volume but the fixed throttle is protective.

findings.what_it_does: POSIX daemonize: the parent waits 5s for the grandchild to publish daemon status before reporting.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The launcher reports failure rc 2 although the grandchild may still come up — a false negative that can trigger operator/automation retries (double-start is fenced by the pid lock).
findings.rationale: 5s of wall clock stands in for 'did the daemon start', which the status file plus process liveness answers directly; on a loaded machine startup routinely exceeds 5s and the launcher lies.

findings.what_it_does: Windows variant of the publish wait; on timeout the spawned worker tree is force-killed.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A daemon slow to publish (AV scanning, cold NTFS) is killed at 180s — startup work destroyed, not just misreported.
findings.rationale: This one kills rather than misreports, making the fixed wall clock genuinely destructive; check that the worker process is alive and progressing instead, or make the kill contingent on liveness failure.

findings.what_it_does: Observation window confirming the published daemon stays alive before declaring success.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Crash-on-boot daemons within 0.5s are caught; slower crashes are reported as successful starts.
findings.rationale: Cheap smoke check; enlarging it delays every start for marginal detection gain.

findings.what_it_does: Grace while reaping the intermediate child during daemonize teardown (also line 164).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Escalates the reap path; nothing user-visible is lost.
findings.rationale: Post-decision cleanup escalation.

findings.what_it_does: Disk headroom reserve required before continuous-state writes proceed.
findings.consequence_when_hit: State writes are refused when free space falls below the reserve, protecting against corrupting a full disk.
findings.rationale: Fail-safe against partial writes on a full disk; bounds are modest and scale-clamped.

findings.what_it_does: Bound and cadence for a launcher waiting for the daemon status record to appear.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The wait returns unsatisfied and the caller reports the daemon as not (yet) up.
findings.rationale: Read-side wait bound; misreport risk is shared with the publish timeout above but this helper itself kills nothing.

findings.what_it_does: Retries the start-daemon critical section when a concurrent starter wins the race (0.02s sleep between attempts).
findings.consequence_when_hit: After 3 lost races the start reports failure; the winning daemon is running anyway.
findings.rationale: Bounded race resolution; losing means someone else started the daemon.

findings.what_it_does: Grace between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when force-stopping a daemon process.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A daemon ignoring SIGTERM is SIGKILLed 0.5s later — termination already decided by the operator's force flag.
findings.rationale: Escalation grace after an explicit force-stop; short is appropriate since the operator asked for force.

findings.what_it_does: How long a graceful stop waits for the daemon to exit before giving up.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Returns rc 2 WITHOUT killing anything unless force is passed; the daemon keeps draining.
findings.rationale: Deliberately non-destructive on timeout — the correct polarity: report, never kill, unless forced.

findings.what_it_does: Cadence of progress heartbeats while waiting for a draining daemon (also line 1592; 0.2s poll at 1593).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Operator sees a still-draining message every 30s; the wait itself is unbounded.
findings.rationale: Observability cadence around an unbounded, work-respecting wait.

findings.what_it_does: A playground candidate section counts as 'substantive' only if its visible text has at least 24 alphanumeric characters (on top of an explicit placeholder-pattern check); failing sections raise stale_template_section and block the candidate from advancing.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Candidate advancement is refused with 'must contain substantive candidate-specific content before advancing' — a legitimately terse but complete section (e.g. a short negative result) is rejected on character count alone.
findings.rationale: This is precisely the arbitrary quality gate the design philosophy flags: 24 chars encodes a human hunch about 'enough prose'. The adjacent checks already catch the real failure modes (verbatim template text, explicit placeholder phrases); content sufficiency beyond that is the reviewer role's judgment, not a character counter's.

findings.what_it_does: Minimum wait between external-work observations during a cadence wait, regardless of how small a poll interval the work registered.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A registrant asking for sub-30s polling is polled no faster than every 30s.
findings.rationale: The floor prevents an agent-registered tiny interval from turning the supervisor into a busy-poll loop that burns rounds; 30s costs essentially nothing against jobs measured in hours.

findings.what_it_does: Maximum time a mission holds its slot waiting in-process between observable external-work facts; on expiry the mission returns paused_external_work (releasing the slot) — the code comment states it 'caps time between observable facts, never the duration of external work'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: After 15 minutes with nothing new to observe, the mission pauses and yields its concurrency slot; the external job keeps running and the mission resumes on later evidence.
findings.rationale: This is the correct architecture under the operator's philosophy: the wall-clock number bounds slot occupancy, not work lifetime, and hitting it kills nothing. 900s is arbitrary but the failure mode is benign (a pause/resume).

findings.what_it_does: Default heartbeat-staleness window: an external-work record whose heartbeat is older than 30 minutes is classified STALLED (dead-owner detection).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The work is reported as stalled to the reviewer/settlement; the mission stops treating it as healthy waiting, so stall counting resumes and the mission can be retired while the underlying GPU job may in fact still be running with a silent heartbeat writer.
findings.rationale: A fixed 30-minute default misclassifies any legitimate job whose wrapper heartbeats less often (long epochs, checkpoint-only touch). The subagent path already derives staleness adaptively at line 291 (max(monitor_interval, cap) * 2); the heartbeat default should similarly derive from the record's declared poll cadence.

findings.symbol: ExternalWorkRecord.poll_after_seconds default (also fallbacks 120.0 at lines 261 and 282)
findings.what_it_does: Default observation cadence for registered external work and background subagents when the registrant did not specify one.
findings.consequence_when_hit: External work is checked every 2 minutes by default; registrants override per record.
findings.rationale: A pure polling default with per-record override and floor/cap clamping; 120s neither burns rounds nor delays evidence meaningfully for jobs that run for hours.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the parsed activity-path and evidence-path lists of an external-work record at 32 entries; extra paths are silently dropped.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Paths beyond the 32nd are never checked for mtime activity, so a job whose only recent writes land in dropped paths looks silent and can be classified stalled despite being alive.
findings.rationale: The cap protects against a runaway registry entry, but silently discarding liveness inputs can produce false stalls on legitimate long jobs — the worst-offender failure mode. At minimum log/flag the drop; better, dedupe to directories or watch the newest N by mtime.

findings.what_it_does: Derives background-subagent staleness as twice the larger of its monitor interval and the cadence cap.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A subagent silent for two full monitoring periods is classified stalled and surfaced as such to the reviewer.
findings.rationale: This is the adaptive pattern the heartbeat default should copy: the timeout scales with the declared cadence rather than being absolute, and the 2x multiplier is the standard missed-two-heartbeats convention.

findings.what_it_does: Sleep-chunk granularity inside a cadence wait so state transitions and stop requests are noticed between full cadence periods.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Stop requests and work-state changes are detected within at most 15 seconds during a wait.
findings.rationale: Pure responsiveness granularity for a local check — cheap, kills nothing, and 15s is a sensible tradeoff between reaction time and wasted wakeups.

findings.what_it_does: Upper bound on the next_step text of an engineer CONTINUE_WORK request; the parser at line 91 returns None (request ignored) when the text exceeds 500 chars.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The engineer's explicit request to continue working is silently discarded — the round settles as if no continuation was requested, purely because the engineer wrote a verbose next step.
findings.rationale: Rejecting the whole request over length is a judgment call encoded as a magic number; truncating the text (or accepting with a marker) preserves intent while still bounding prompt size. Silent drop of a control signal is the smell.

findings.what_it_does: Env-fallback default for the decision-progress timeout; 0 means the timeout is disabled unless an operator opts in via env.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Never fires by default; when enabled by env it bounds how long a turn may run without a decision.
findings.rationale: A disabled-by-default wall-clock kill switch is exactly the right polarity under the operator's philosophy: long-running legitimate work is never killed unless someone explicitly configures it.

findings.what_it_does: Env-fallback default for the hard-idle watchdog (kills a turn producing no output for N seconds); 0 disables it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Never fires by default; when env-enabled, a silent turn is aborted and retried (retries capped at 2 by round_execution.py:460).
findings.rationale: Off-by-default is correct: an idle-output watchdog can misfire on legitimately quiet long computations, so requiring explicit opt-in protects long GPU/compile work.

findings.what_it_does: Number of consecutive rounds in which the engineer produced no output at all before the mission ends with status no_progress.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Mission terminates as no_progress after 2 consecutive empty engineer rounds; any output resets the counter.
findings.rationale: This is a loop-stopper against burning LLM calls on a dead engineer, not a wall-clock kill: it triggers only on literally empty rounds, which no legitimate long-running work produces (external work is tracked separately and waiting resets stall logic).

findings.what_it_does: Consecutive reviewer verdicts with explicit FORWARD_PROGRESS=false (semantic stall) before the mission ends with no_progress; rescaled by _fit_stall_guard to stay reachable within max_rounds.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Mission retires after 4 explicit no-progress judgments in a row; the streak resets when the mission is blocked on healthy external work ('waiting is not stalling').
findings.rationale: A semantic loop-stopper driven only by the reviewer's explicit judgment, with the healthy-wait exemption codified after a documented incident (7 missions retired in 90 minutes for waiting on healthy jobs). It cannot kill legitimate long-running work.

findings.what_it_does: Round count at which an anti-livelock escalation hint is injected into the reviewer prompt; guard-rescaled in __post_init__ to stay below max_rounds.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The reviewer is told to escalate/decide rather than keep granting continue verdicts; nothing is killed and the mission keeps running.
findings.rationale: Advisory-only escalation that costs nothing when wrong and bounds livelock when right; 12 is arbitrary but the mechanism degrades gracefully because it only changes prompt content.

findings.what_it_does: Round count at which the stronger escalation directive is injected (still prompt-level, still not a kill).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Reviewer receives a hard escalation directive demanding resolution; the mission continues under reviewer authority.
findings.rationale: Same graceful-degradation argument as soft_round_limit: it steers judgment rather than terminating work, and it is guard-rescaled against max_rounds so it stays coherent.

findings.what_it_does: Consecutive reviewer-backend infrastructure failures (classified from fatal_error patterns) tolerated before the mission fails loud with status error instead of running the completion gate blind.
findings.consequence_when_hit: After just 2 consecutive backend failures the whole mission errors out — even though the expensive engineer work already completed and the failure is transient infrastructure.
findings.rationale: Failing loud instead of reviewing blind is correct, but 2 attempts spaced 15s apart means a ~30-second API blip can abandon hours of completed engineer work. Retry budget should scale with the cost of the work being settled (e.g., more attempts with growing backoff before surrendering).

findings.what_it_does: Fixed sleep between reviewer-backend retry attempts (slept at round_reviewer.py:642 and round_execution.py:547); no exponential growth.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Retries hammer a failing backend every 15s and exhaust the tiny threshold quickly during any outage longer than ~30 seconds.
findings.rationale: Flat 15s backoff paired with threshold 2 encodes 'give up after 30 seconds of outage'. Exponential backoff with a cap (or jittered retry over minutes) would survive routine transient outages without burning extra LLM calls.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback default for how many turns a resumable role session (reviewer capsule) may accumulate before being recycled to a fresh session.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The role session is discarded and rebuilt from the static rubric, losing conversational continuity, purely on turn count.
findings.rationale: Turn count is a weak proxy for the thing actually being bounded (context size); the companion role_session_max_input_tokens knob already measures that directly. Recycling should key off the token budget, making the turn count redundant.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback default for the input-token budget at which a resumable role session is recycled to fresh.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Session recycled before overflowing the backend context window; the static rubric is re-sent and prior thread continuity is lost, but resume state is designed for this.
findings.rationale: This bound exists to stay under real model context limits and is env-overridable per backend; the fallback of 120k is a reasonable safety margin for current models, and hitting it degrades gracefully by design (fresh session with full static prompt).

findings.what_it_does: Keeps only the newest 8 pending secret-guard notes; older undelivered notes are silently deleted before being surfaced.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If more than 8 secret-guard events accumulate between deliveries, the oldest warnings are dropped without any record that they existed.
findings.rationale: A bounded queue prevents unbounded prompt growth from a pathological note flood, and secret-guard notes are advisories whose newest instances matter most; still, a dropped-count marker would be a cheap improvement.

findings.what_it_does: When a turn failure was caused by the hard-idle watchdog, the fresh-session retry threshold is clamped to at most 2 regardless of the operator-configured value.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A turn that is legitimately quiet (long in-turn computation with no streamed output) gets at most 2 retries and then fails the round, even if the operator configured a larger retry budget.
findings.rationale: Silently overriding explicit operator configuration with a hardcoded 2 is the design smell the audit targets; the clamp's intent (don't replay an expensive turn that keeps idling) is sound, but the cap should respect config or be its own named, configurable knob.

findings.what_it_does: Only the last 3 round verdicts are summarized into the reviewer's context; older verdict history is omitted.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The reviewer judging round N cannot see verdicts before round N-3, so slow oscillation patterns (repeating a direction rejected 5 rounds ago) are invisible in this block.
findings.rationale: Bounded history keeps the per-round delta prompt small, and longer-horizon memory is carried separately via prev_review_summary and the incremental re-review boundary; widening the raw window would mostly duplicate that channel.

findings.what_it_does: Each prior verdict's reason string is truncated to 600 chars when summarized into the reviewer's history block.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The tail of a long prior reason is silently cut; nuance beyond 600 chars does not reach the next reviewer round.
findings.rationale: This is a summary-of-history block, not primary evidence — the full verdict already drove its own round's settlement, and reasons are themselves capped at 5000 chars upstream. 600 chars of headline per round is a sane prompt-budget tradeoff.

findings.what_it_does: At the soft round limit, the mission is considered stalled for escalation purposes if neither of the last 2 verdicts explicitly affirmed forward progress — a window hardcoded independently of stall_threshold.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Escalation semantics engage after only 2 non-affirming verdicts, including verdicts that merely omitted FORWARD_PROGRESS, a stricter and differently-shaped test than the configured 4-strike explicit-false stall_threshold.
findings.rationale: Two stall definitions now coexist: the configured explicit-signal streak and this hardcoded absence-of-affirmation window. Tying the window to the config (or reusing the semantic streak counter) removes a hidden second threshold that can surprise operators who tuned stall_threshold.

findings.what_it_does: Processed chat event ids are remembered for 24h and pruned on write; within the window a redelivered/replayed platform event is recognized and skipped.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An event redelivered more than 24h later would re-execute its command — far beyond any platform's actual redelivery window, so effectively never.
findings.rationale: Without the ledger, Feishu redelivery and WebSocket replay would run the same /add twice, enqueueing duplicate missions; without the retention bound the ledger file grows forever. 24h is generously above real redelivery windows and self-prunes without a scheduler — exactly the documented trade.

findings.what_it_does: Chunk size for Feishu card replies (the platform accepts far more; 4000 is chosen so cards scroll well on a phone). chunk_html splits at this size — content is never truncated.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A long reply arrives as multiple cards; no data loss.
findings.rationale: A UX-motivated split size with lossless behavior — the module exists specifically because the old code truncated instead of splitting. TELEGRAM_LIMIT=4096 alongside it is the platform's hard protocol cap, excluded as a protocol constant.

findings.what_it_does: Default per-field cap for MissionBrief projection: acceptance criteria, reviewer reason, and next_action are each whitespace-collapsed and hard-sliced to 600 characters with no truncation marker.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A reviewer's 'why this round failed' or the acceptance check is silently cut mid-sentence in the brief the next round is steered by.
findings.rationale: These fields carry the decisive round-to-round signal in a long campaign; silent mid-sentence truncation of a review reason can misdirect the next round. Cap should come from the brief's overall budget and truncation should be marked (an ellipsis at minimum).

findings.what_it_does: Caps list projections in MissionBrief — changed-surface artifacts, remaining-work items, and tools/resources — at 6 entries each, silently dropping the rest.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A frontier with more than 6 remaining-work items shows only the first 6; the continuation round does not learn the others exist.
findings.rationale: Dropping remaining-work items without a '(+N more)' marker can make a continuation believe the missing conditions are fewer than they are. Either mark the elision or size the list from the brief budget.

findings.symbol: engineer_summary brief cap (with the stored-handoff cap [:4000] at lines 366/422)
findings.value: 1200 chars in MissionBrief; 4000 chars persisted per round handoff
findings.what_it_does: The Engineer's own account of a round is stored truncated to 4000 chars in the round handoff file and further truncated to 1200 chars when projected into the next round's MissionBrief.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The 4000-char cut is permanent (the handoff file is the durable record); the 1200-char cut silently hides the tail of the prior round's account from the fresh continuation the docstring says should not have to infer work.
findings.rationale: The whole point of carrying the Engineer account (per the module docstring) is that a fresh continuation should not re-infer prior work; a fixed 1200-char slice of a 4000-char stored account undermines that silently. Derive both from the consuming prompt budget and mark truncation.

findings.what_it_does: Caps both the paths extracted from a completion message (referenced_delivery_paths) and the targets included in a terminal delivery receipt; candidates past the sixth are silently dropped.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Reviewer-named evidence files or declared vertical deliverables beyond 6 do not appear in the completion receipt the operator opens.
