findings.rationale: The candidate set is already bounded by construction (only reviewer-named artifacts and contract-declared deliverables, deduplicated, safety-filtered) — an arbitrary 6 on top of that silently hides evidence. If a bound is wanted for phone rendering, let the render surface decide how many to show and keep the receipt complete.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the completion summary embedded in the delivery receipt to 1200 characters with no marker (title 240, status/review_status 80, why 500 are similar sibling caps).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The operator-facing summary of a completed campaign task is silently cut.
findings.rationale: Receipt fields are consumed by chat surfaces that already split long messages; a fixed silent cut is unnecessary. Minor compared to the targets cap, but the same silent-truncation pattern.

findings.what_it_does: Rotates events.jsonl to events.jsonl.1 when it exceeds 100 MiB; every previous generation is renamed aside (.2, .3, ...) rather than deleted, so no event is ever lost. A 1 MiB floor is enforced on custom values at line 180.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Rotation only — the audit trail is preserved in full across generations; tail readers keep working via events.jsonl.1.
findings.rationale: This is the good kind of cap: it bounds single-file size (keeping reverse-tail reads and rg scans fast) while explicitly refusing to truncate or drop data. Without it a long campaign's event log becomes one multi-GB file that every status/journal projection must seek through.

findings.what_it_does: Failure-experience retrieval reads only the last 1 MB of failure_experiences.jsonl; anything earlier in the file is never a retrieval candidate.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older failure capsules silently fall out of the retrievable memory — they remain on disk but the direct/transfer/analogy channels can never surface them, so hard-won lessons age out by byte offset, not relevance.
findings.rationale: Bounding a per-prompt scan is reasonable, but the bound should track the store (scan enough bytes to cover a target number of capsules, or maintain a compact index) rather than a fixed megabyte that means '~250 capsules' today and 'last week only' once capsules grow. For a system whose pitch is learning from failures, a silent 1 MB horizon on that learning is a real policy choice.

findings.what_it_does: Within the scanned tail bytes, only the last 256 JSONL records are parsed into candidate rows.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Same silent horizon as the byte cap, in record units; combined with annotation rows (which share the budget) the effective experience pool can be much smaller than 256.
findings.rationale: Same reasoning as _DEFAULT_SCAN_BYTES — the two caps jointly define how far back failure memory reaches, and annotations consuming record slots makes the effective window unpredictable. Derive from desired candidate count.

findings.symbol: _clean_text default limit (representative of per-field write-time caps: 4000 default; 200/300/500/800/1000 per field)
findings.what_it_does: Truncates every failure-capsule text field at write time (narrative/lessons at 4000 via default, title 500, mission_id 300, artifact refs 800, concepts 200, etc.), appending an ellipsis.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The stored capsule is permanently truncated — the full narrative can never be recovered from the store, only from raw artifacts.
findings.rationale: The module's contract is explicitly 'bounded capsules; prose is primary and facets are retrieval hints' with raw artifacts kept as lazy refs — the caps are what keep the store scannable in one tail read. Truncation is visible (ellipsis) and full evidence remains reachable via artifact_refs. The specific values are judgment calls but the bounding mechanism is the design.

findings.symbol: retrieve max_entries default (and hardcoded candidate pool of 64 at line 326)
findings.what_it_does: Mixes at most 4 failure capsules (one recent, one direct-match, one transfer, one reserved exploratory-analogy slot) chosen from the 64 most recent experiences into role prompts.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Only 4 prior failures inform a mission regardless of how many are relevant; the pool for scoring is the newest 64.
findings.rationale: The 4-slot channel mix is a thoughtful design, but both numbers encode 'how much failure memory a mission gets' and should scale with prompt budget and store size. The code itself is careful to say facets 'never reject a new attempt', so widening this adaptively is safe.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the rendered failure-experience context block; when exceeded, the render returns the first max_chars-1 characters with a trailing ellipsis, cutting mid-capsule.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Later capsules (and possibly the tail of the current one) are silently dropped from the prompt.
findings.rationale: Same prompt-budget family as memory.py's 6_000 defaults (memory.py lines 2375/2899 pass the same number). One knob derived from model context should govern these, not four copies of 6_000.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds every Feishu open-platform call: token fetch, per-chunk card send, reaction add/remove. Failure returns None (debug log); send() drops the chunk, token failure drops the whole reply with a warning.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Operator-facing reply content is silently lost on a slow/failed API call; no retry anywhere in the send path.
findings.rationale: The socket bound protects the worker thread from hanging indefinitely (commands run under a per-chat lock, so a hang would freeze the whole chat). As with Telegram, the number is fine; the silent-drop-without-retry behavior around it is the actual weakness.

findings.what_it_does: Treats a cached tenant access token as stale one minute before its actual expiry so a long-running command never sends with a token that expires mid-flight.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A fresh token is fetched slightly early; one extra API call every ~2 hours.
findings.rationale: Cheap, standard clock-skew/latency margin against a 7200s token lifetime. Making it proportional to expire would be marginally cleaner but the failure it prevents (401 mid-send, reply dropped) is real and the cost is negligible.

findings.what_it_does: Assumes the documented 2-hour Feishu token lifetime when the API response omits the expire field.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If Feishu ever issued a shorter-lived token without an expire field, the cache would serve an expired token and sends would fail (silently, per the _request behavior) until the cache aged out.
findings.rationale: Fallback mirrors the platform's documented constant; the field is essentially always present. A safer fallback would be a small value forcing re-fetch, but the practical risk is nil.

findings.what_it_does: Kills the optional rg subprocess used to find sparse journal events in huge JSONL files if it runs longer than 10s; the function then returns None and the caller falls back to the pure-Python reverse chunk reader.
findings.consequence_when_hit: No data loss and no abandoned work — only the fast path is abandoned; the slower fallback produces the same result.
findings.rationale: A bounded fast path with a correct fallback is exactly where a wall-clock timeout is legitimate: rg hanging on a pathological file must not block a status query, and the timeout changes performance, never results.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the per-instance memo cache of total_cost_since(ts) results; oldest entries are evicted FIFO when more than 32 distinct window timestamps are queried.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An evicted window's next query re-scans the journal files — a recompute, no behavioral change.
findings.rationale: Prevents unbounded memory growth in a long-lived daemon that queries many distinct cost windows. Eviction cost is a re-read; correctness is signature-checked either way.

findings.what_it_does: Default number of journal-relevant events returned when a caller does not specify how far back to read.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Callers relying on the default see only the 20 newest journal entries; older history exists on disk but is not surfaced.
findings.rationale: A read-window default that silently shapes what 'recent history' means to every default caller (status cards, layer detection). Callers with real needs already pass n; the default should be derived from the consuming surface (e.g. how many entries the prompt/display budget can hold) rather than a fixed 20.

findings.what_it_does: An item found 'running' after the owning process died is reset to 'pending' for retry; after being orphaned more than 3 times it is marked 'failed' permanently (terminal status, cannot be resurrected per IllegalStateTransition).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The backlog item is failed with 'orphaned: previous process did not finish (exceeded 3 retries)'. Work is abandoned, but only after three confirmed process deaths on the same item.
findings.rationale: Classic poison-pill breaker: an item whose execution reliably crashes the daemon would otherwise be re-dispatched forever, burning budget in a crash loop. The docstring is explicit that this counts confirmed process deaths, not live work, so it never kills a running mission. Whether the count is 3 or 5 is a mild judgment call, but the bound itself must exist.

findings.value: 3 entries surfaced, scanning the last 30 journal events
findings.what_it_does: Controls how much prior-mission journal history is injected as non-authoritative memory context into role prompts: look back 30 journal events, surface the newest 3.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Everything older than the 3 newest entries is invisible to the agent's memory context — silently, with no marker that history was elided.
findings.rationale: How much memory an autonomous researcher gets is a consequential judgment call encoded as '3'. It should scale with the consuming model's context budget and the campaign's length (a 200-mission campaign and a 5-mission one get identical memory), or at minimum be configured alongside the other prompt-budget knobs.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the operator's identity card to its first 600 characters before injecting it into the memory prelude of engineer/reviewer prompts.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Identity/policy text beyond 600 chars is silently cut — an operator who writes a detailed identity card has the tail dropped from every prompt with no indication.
findings.rationale: Silent truncation of operator-authored directives is the kind of quiet data loss the audit targets. The cap should derive from the overall prompt budget, and truncation should at least be marked so the agent (and operator) know the card was cut.

findings.what_it_does: Auto-quarantines a project when spent_usd/budget_usd >= 0.80 and no paper draft exists. Quarantine hard-stops dispatch: the daemon refuses tokens until a human resumes or archives, and the state persists across restarts.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The project is halted (LifecycleEvent to QUARANTINED). No work is killed mid-flight, but no new missions dispatch for it.
findings.rationale: This is a budget guard, not a wall-clock timeout — it stops further LLM spend on a project about to exhaust an operator-set budget without its expected artifact. The module deliberately removed the old time-in-stage auto-quarantines (7d/14d/21d, now advisory-only signals) and kept exactly this one; the fraction is overridable per-project via ProjectStatus.quarantine_budget_fraction, and a human resume path exists. Without it a stuck project burns the remaining 20% before the hard cap. The 'no draft' criterion does encode 'the expected artifact is a paper', which is worth noting, but the mechanism is protective.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the lifecycle sidecar's persisted transition history at the most recent 200 LifecycleEvents.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Transitions older than the newest 200 are silently dropped from lifecycle.json (the authoritative current state is unaffected; the event log retains the full record elsewhere).
findings.rationale: Bounds a JSON file that is re-read and re-written whole under a lock on every persist; 200 transitions is far beyond any realistic project's lifecycle churn, and full history survives in events.jsonl. Unbounded growth here would slow every locked write.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the living RESEARCH_PLAN.md projection into the Planner prompt; beyond it the head is kept, a visible truncation notice instructing the Planner to return a pruned PLAN_UPDATE is inserted, and the Next-milestone section tail (itself capped at 2000 chars, line 91) is preserved.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Middle sections of the plan (typically Established results / Dead ends bodies) are cut from the Planner's view for that cycle, with an explicit marker and a self-healing instruction.
findings.rationale: Well-engineered truncation (visible, self-correcting, milestone-preserving), but 8000 chars is a fixed stand-in for 'the Planner's dynamic context allowance' — it should be derived from the actual model/prompt budget so a larger-context Planner sees its whole plan and a smaller one isn't overrun.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the hypotheses + next-milestone excerpt projected into mission (Engineer) prompts; over the cap, budget is apportioned (milestone floor max(500, limit//3), line 115) and both sections are ellipsis-truncated.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Central hypotheses and the milestone are silently shortened in the Engineer's brief — the agent doing the actual experiments may see truncated hypotheses.
findings.rationale: Same prompt-budget family as the Planner cap; 2000 chars for the scientific core of a mission brief is a judgment call that should scale with the mission prompt's real budget. The internal 500/limit//3 apportioning is fine mechanics once the outer number is principled.

findings.what_it_does: Keeps a role with an unmatched agent.io.start showing as active for up to 50 minutes in the cockpit role panel, deliberately sized to exceed 'the runner's default 45-minute hard-idle window'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Display only: past the window a silent-but-alive provider turn shows as inactive/'Waiting'. No work is affected.
findings.rationale: The number is a hardcoded shadow of another component's timeout (45 min + 5 margin, per its own comment). If the runner's idle window changes, this silently drifts and the panel lies again — derive it from the runner's configured value instead of re-encoding it here.

findings.symbol: role_activity active_window_s default (with STALE_LABEL_WINDOW_S=180.0 at line 275)
findings.value: 90.0 seconds active window; 180.0 seconds label-decay window
findings.what_it_does: A role is shown 'active' only if it owns the most recent activity event fresher than 90s; a non-active role's last label decays to 'idle' once its event is older than 180s.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Display only: labels flip to idle/inactive in the cockpit. No dispatch or mission behavior reads these.
findings.rationale: Pure presentation freshness windows with documented reasoning (decay > active so terminal labels linger briefly). Nothing breaks if tweaked, but they prevent the panel from freezing stale verbose labels; not worth adaptivity machinery. Related: the _tail_jsonl limit=500 at line 26 bounds the panel's event scan — same display-only, bounded-read character.

findings.what_it_does: Refuses to deliver the front-door Manager's fast-path reply to the operator when it exceeds 1600 characters; only a routing diagnostic is emitted.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The reply is silently withheld from the operator — they get nothing, not a truncated or split message. Only a 'reply exceeded 1600 chars; not delivered' diagnostic lands in the failure sink.
findings.rationale: The chat transports (chunk_html in life/chat/render.py) already split arbitrarily long messages safely, so length is not a delivery constraint. If the gate's real intent is 'a huge reply means the classifier hallucinated a work product into the fast path', that is a shape judgment an LLM route should make, not a magic character count that discards content wholesale.

findings.what_it_does: Drops an operator steering directive (control == 'steer') when the extracted directive exceeds 1600 characters.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A live-mission steering instruction from the operator is silently not delivered to the running mission; only a diagnostic is logged. The operator believes they steered the campaign and nothing happened.
findings.rationale: Worse than the reply gate: this discards operator intent directed at long-running work. There is no downstream constraint requiring 1600 chars — the directive is written into mission state, not a chat platform. Deliver it whole; if bounding is ever needed, derive from the consuming prompt's budget.

findings.what_it_does: Keeps only the 20 most recent deduplicated backlog item ids affected by the active runtime-failure circuit in its state file.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older affected item ids drop out of the circuit record (occurrence_count still counts them; the event log retains full history).
findings.rationale: Bounds a state file that is rewritten on every occurrence of a crash-looping runtime failure; 20 ids is ample for diagnosis and the count field preserves magnitude. Note the circuit itself is count-free by design — it opens on the first fingerprint and holds dispatch until a fact changes, which matches the operator philosophy (no arbitrary retry threshold).

findings.what_it_does: Default sleep between checks in _wait_idle while missions are running (config field, hardcoded default).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Supervisor re-checks mission/queue state every 5 seconds; pure polling latency, no work impact.
findings.rationale: Already a config field with a benign default; 5s is cheap local polling. No reason to change.

findings.what_it_does: Consecutive failures by one subagent family (within the window) before the F6 circuit breaker quarantines that family (config default).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The family is blocked from re-dispatch; docstring documents the pathology it fixes (SWE-bench full-canary retried ~20x over 2 days pre-fix).
findings.rationale: Battle-tested loop-stopper with a documented incident behind it, and already configurable. The hardcoded default is the sensible conservative choice.

findings.what_it_does: Sliding window within which family failures count toward the F6 streak (config default).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Failures older than 72h stop counting, so a family that failed days ago gets a fresh chance; failures inside 72h accumulate toward quarantine.
findings.rationale: Configurable with a defensible default; window semantics (old failures age out) err on the side of retrying work rather than permanently banning it — the right bias per the operator philosophy.

findings.what_it_does: Starting delay for the exponential idle backoff the supervisor sleeps between planner cycles when there is no work; doubles each idle cycle (_idle_cycle.py:216-228).
findings.consequence_when_hit: First no-work cycle waits 15s before re-polling for events/work; only delays idle polling, never running missions.
findings.rationale: A sane base for an exponential poll backoff; it only shapes idle-loop latency and burns no LLM calls. Nothing legitimate is killed or abandoned.

findings.what_it_does: Cap on the exponential idle backoff (comment: caps event-poll latency while idle; never limits mission work).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Idle supervisor polls for new events/work at most every 5 minutes; worst-case 5-minute latency reacting to an external unblock.
findings.rationale: Bounds worst-case wake latency without limiting mission work — exactly the good kind of cap. However it is also reused at _planning_context.py:1409 as an unrelated operator-wait re-grant cadence (see separate finding); the reuse, not the value, is the smell.

findings.what_it_does: Minimum interval between repeated 'planner idle/waiting' journal entries while waiting on the same blocker (_idle_cycle.py:301).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Duplicate idle heartbeats within 30 minutes are suppressed; the wait stays observable at 30-minute cadence instead of spamming the journal.
findings.rationale: Journal spam poisons planner context (tail windows are bounded); suppressing repeats is load-bearing. 30 minutes is a reasonable observability cadence with no work-killing consequence.

findings.what_it_does: Minimum interval between repeated lifecycle-block event emissions.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Repeat lifecycle-block notifications inside 30 minutes are deduplicated.
findings.rationale: Same anti-spam role as the idle heartbeat. Note: _lifecycle.py:32 hardcodes its own private copy of this same value instead of importing it — that duplicate should be deleted (see _lifecycle.py finding).

findings.what_it_does: Consecutive replan_requested outcomes on one backlog item before the supervisor stops resetting it to pending; env-overridable via ARGUS_SKILL_CONSECUTIVE_REPLAN_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD (lines 54-73), this is the hardcoded fallback.
findings.consequence_when_hit: At _mission_execution_settlement.py:944-948 the item is escalated to a terminal no_progress failure (mark_failed) instead of being re-dispatched.
findings.rationale: Classic loop-stopper: prevents infinite replan/dispatch LLM burn on a refuted node. Already env-overridable, and the quarantine is soft (failures age out of the recent-history window and become re-proposable).

findings.what_it_does: Number of trailing journal entries scanned (_mission_execution_settlement.py:510) to count an item's consecutive replans for the escalation threshold.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If more than 100 journal entries land between an item's replans (chatty campaign, many parallel missions), earlier replans fall out of the window and the streak silently undercounts, delaying or defeating the escalation breaker.
findings.rationale: The breaker's correctness depends on journal chattiness, which varies by campaign. Counting replans per item id directly (or scanning until the item's last non-replan outcome) would make the breaker exact instead of window-dependent.

findings.what_it_does: Idle planner cycles stuck on the same blocker fingerprint before the stall-breaker dispatches one bounded verification-probe mission to re-test the blocker belief (_planning_context.py:2004-2005).
findings.consequence_when_hit: One probe mission (iteration_max_cycles=1) is enqueued to check whether the remembered blocker is still real, so stale beliefs cannot idle the campaign forever.
findings.rationale: This is an anti-stall mechanism, not a work-killer: it spends one bounded mission to escape a potentially-false wait. 4 cycles plus the 1800s cooldown keeps probe cost negligible.

findings.what_it_does: Planner-waiting cycles before the Manager is asked to re-adjudicate the wait (used _planning_cycle.py:680, 697, 747).
findings.consequence_when_hit: After 4 consecutive waits on the same reconciliation key, a Manager reconcile pass runs to confirm or break the wait.
findings.rationale: Second layer of the stall-breaker; bounded extra LLM cost in exchange for not trusting a possibly stale wait indefinitely. Value is a judgment call but any small integer works; not worth config surface.

findings.what_it_does: Minimum wall-clock gap between verification probes for the same blocker fingerprint (_planning_context.py:2034-2038).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A repeat probe within 30 minutes is skipped; the planner keeps waiting instead of re-probing.
findings.rationale: Direct LLM/mission-burn limiter: without it a persistent blocker would trigger a probe every few idle cycles. Cost of being wrong is only added wait latency, never lost work.

findings.what_it_does: Consecutive no-progress mission settlements before a LIFE_PLANNER_STALL_ESCALATION operator event is emitted; counter then resets so it re-fires every 3 (_planning_context.py:2144-2150).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Operator gets an escalation event; no work is stopped or state changed beyond the counter reset.
findings.rationale: Purely observational: it only controls operator-notification cadence. Harmless wherever it is set; 3 gives early signal without noise.

findings.what_it_does: Times a replanned item may have all of its proposed replacement tasks rejected by the enqueue filter before the item is terminal (_planning_cycle_enqueue.py:1067).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Item is mark_failed and the plan settles to PLAN_TERMINAL_IDLE instead of looping planner->filter->reject forever.
findings.rationale: Loop-stopper against a planner that keeps proposing duplicates of existing backlog items — each loop is a full planner LLM call. Failure is visible (terminal status plus event), not silent.

findings.what_it_does: Rounds of Manager-feedback-driven replanning on one item before intake gives up (_planning_cycle_intake.py:236).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Plan settles to PLAN_TERMINAL_IDLE; the Manager/Planner disagreement loop is broken instead of burning alternating LLM calls.
findings.rationale: Breaks a two-agent argument loop that would otherwise never converge. Three rounds is enough to fix genuine misunderstandings; beyond that the disagreement is structural and needs escalation, not retries.

findings.what_it_does: Compatibility duplicate of the failure-quarantine window also defined at _planner_orchestration.py:21.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Same behavior as the primary constant today; the two copies can silently diverge under future edits.
findings.rationale: Re-export the single definition instead of restating the literal. The policy critique lives on the _planner_orchestration.py:21 finding.

findings.what_it_does: Scans the last 80 journal entries for the most recent successful mission_complete when building the terminal project delivery receipt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If more than 80 journal entries landed after the last successful mission (long wind-down, chatty settlement), the terminal receipt silently reports no completed mission found despite one existing.
findings.rationale: A terminal artifact — the campaign's final receipt — should not depend on journal chattiness. Query by event type without an arbitrary window, or persist the last-success pointer as it happens.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the normalized blocker fingerprint (the identity key for waiting contracts, probe cooldowns, and idle-cycle counting) at 500 chars.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Two distinct blockers whose normalized text shares the first 500 chars collapse into one identity, merging their wait/probe/cooldown state.
findings.rationale: Identity keys need a bound, 500 normalized chars is generous, and the failure mode (rare fingerprint collision) degrades to slightly-wrong probe dedup, never lost work. Appending a hash of the full text would make collisions impossible at trivial cost if desired.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback for ARGUS_SKILL_DAEMON_IDLE_EXIT_MIN: minutes of continuous idleness before the daemon exits cleanly; 0 disables auto-exit (_maybe_idle_timeout, lines 251-280).
findings.consequence_when_hit: With default 0 the daemon never self-terminates on idleness; only an explicit env value enables the exit, and even then it fires only when fully idle (no missions running).
findings.rationale: The dangerous direction (killing work) is impossible: exit only triggers when idle and only when the operator opts in via env. The 0 default is exactly the policy the operator wants.

findings.what_it_does: Maximum operator inbox messages ingested per idle cycle.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Messages beyond 10 wait for the next cycle; they are deferred, not dropped.
findings.rationale: Bounds per-cycle context injection without losing data — overflow drains on subsequent cycles at worst a few minutes later. Backlogs of >10 unread operator messages are rare.

findings.what_it_does: Private module copy of LIFECYCLE_BLOCK_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS from _constants.py:12, used at lines 267-270 to suppress repeat lifecycle-block emissions.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Behaviorally identical to the shared constant today, but changing the value in _constants.py silently does not change this path.
findings.rationale: Pure duplication — import the shared constant. The value itself is fine (see _constants.py:12 finding); the duplicate is the defect.

findings.what_it_does: Forces repair-capability missions to a single engineer round in direct workflow mode (also hardcoded at line 732).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A repair that genuinely needs multiple engineer rounds settles after one round and must surface as a normal failure/replan rather than iterating in place.
findings.rationale: Repair missions run outside normal review scaffolding, so an unbounded repair loop would be the most dangerous burn in the scope; one round then re-adjudication through the standard machinery is the safe shape. Note the literal appears twice — worth a named constant.

findings.what_it_does: Whitespace-normalizes then truncates the mission summary to 1200 chars before writing it to the durable receipt/journal.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The durable record of what a mission accomplished loses everything past 1200 chars, with no ellipsis and no full-text copy; downstream planner history rendering then truncates further to 1800 chars per entry.
findings.rationale: This truncation is at the storage layer, so the data is unrecoverable — unlike rendering-time caps. Store the full summary (or a pointer to it) and truncate only at render time where token budgets actually apply.

findings.what_it_does: Caps delivery paths extracted from the mission summary for the delivery receipt at 12.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A mission that produced more than 12 referenced artifacts gets a receipt listing only the first 12; the rest are silently absent from the durable delivery record.
findings.rationale: Delivery receipts are the campaign's proof of work; silently dropping artifacts corrupts that record. Record all paths durably and cap only rendered previews, or at minimum record an overflow count.

findings.what_it_does: Second [:12] slice on delivery candidate paths during receipt assembly.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Same silent artifact drop as the limit=12 above, applied at a second point in the same pipeline.
findings.rationale: Duplicated magic cap in one flow; whatever replaces the limit=12 finding should unify both into a single named policy.

findings.what_it_does: Journal-tail window defining the no-progress failure quarantine: items that failed within the last 20 journal entries are blocked from re-proposal; older failures become re-proposable.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Quarantine lifetime is measured in journal entries, not time or attempts: a chatty journal expires quarantines in minutes (re-burning LLM calls on known-dead items), a quiet one quarantines nearly forever.
findings.rationale: The unit is wrong, not just the number — journal chattiness varies wildly across campaigns. Quarantine should key on time and/or intervening successful missions rather than raw entry count. Also duplicated at _core.py:126 (drift risk).

findings.what_it_does: Only after 2+ consecutive idle cycles does the planner prompt get the CURRENT-REALITY CHECK digest prefix.
findings.consequence_when_hit: First idle cycle plans without the extra digest; from the second onward the planner is pushed to re-verify reality instead of trusting remembered blockers.
findings.rationale: Saves digest-construction and prompt-token cost on the common single-idle-cycle case while guaranteeing the reality check kicks in almost immediately. Any small value works; not worth surface area.

findings.what_it_does: Shows at most 12 pipeline stages in the planner's reality digest.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Stages beyond 12 are silently omitted from the digest.
findings.rationale: Same silent-drop pattern as the blockers cap; add an overflow count or prioritize non-terminal stages so the planner sees what is actually in flight.

findings.what_it_does: 5-second wall-clock cap on `git status --porcelain=v1` when building the planner's current-reality digest.
findings.consequence_when_hit: changed_paths degrade to '(clean or unavailable)' in the digest; the planner cycle proceeds normally — nothing is killed or abandoned.
findings.rationale: The only wall-clock timeout in the entire scope, and it is the benign kind: it protects the planner loop from a wedged git (NFS, lock contention) and degrades gracefully to a labeled unknown. Worst case on a huge repo is a slightly less informed digest.

findings.what_it_does: Stops collecting 'open questions / blockers' lines from checkpoint files after 8 for the planner's reality digest.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Blockers beyond the first 8 are silently absent from the digest, with no '+N more' marker — the planner cannot know they exist.
findings.rationale: Silent truncation of exactly the information the reality-check digest exists to surface. At minimum append a '+N more' count (as changed_preview at line 190-192 already does); >8 real blockers is also itself a signal worth showing the planner.

findings.what_it_does: Shows at most 12 changed paths in the planner reality digest, then appends a '+N more' overflow count (lines 191-192).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Planner sees the first 12 changed paths plus an explicit count of the remainder — truncation is visible, not silent.
findings.rationale: This is the correct truncation pattern (cap plus overflow count) and is the model the sibling caps at lines 112 and 185 should copy. Reported for completeness as a genuine hardcoded window.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback literal used when reading subagent_family_failure_streak_limit from config raises (paired with window_hours=72.0 fallback at line 249).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A malformed config silently reverts the F6 breaker to 3-in-72h instead of the configured policy.
findings.rationale: Third copy of the same policy pair. Import the config-class defaults (or fail loudly) instead of restating the literals here — silent divergence from configured policy is the failure mode this invites.

findings.what_it_does: Number of recent terminal missions rendered in detail into the planner's context.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The planner reasons about only the last 3 mission outcomes; older outcomes exist only via the coarse campaign tally, so patterns spanning >3 missions (alternating failures, slow drift) are invisible to it.
findings.rationale: This is decision-quality-critical LLM context being capped by a fixed count. Budget it in tokens against the model's window (e.g. fill up to N tokens of history) rather than a fixed 3, which was presumably chosen for a smaller context era.

findings.what_it_does: Per-entry character truncation (with ellipsis) of each rendered mission-history entry in planner context.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Long mission summaries lose their tail — often the reviewer verdict or final error detail, since summaries are typically chronological — degrading the planner's understanding of why a mission ended.
findings.rationale: Silent tail-drop of decision context. Prefer structure-aware compression (keep outcome/verdict fields whole, truncate the middle) or a token budget shared with _PLANNER_HISTORY_COUNT.

findings.what_it_does: Reads the last 4096 journal entries to compute the campaign tally (missions attempted/succeeded/failed) shown to the planner.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Campaigns whose journal exceeds 4096 entries get a silently understated tally; the planner believes fewer missions have run than actually have.
findings.rationale: Correctness of a count should not depend on a tail window. Maintain running counters incrementally (or persist the tally) so the window is only a rendering concern; long campaigns are exactly when accurate tallies matter most.

findings.what_it_does: Scans the last 64 journal entries for recent-activity signals when rendering planner context.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Activity older than 64 entries is treated as absent; on chatty journals the recency horizon shrinks to minutes.
findings.rationale: Entry-count windows conflate chattiness with time. A time-based horizon (or typed-event filter before windowing) gives stable semantics across campaigns.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the sealed context packet to 600 chars when rendering it into planner context.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Everything past 600 chars of the packet is silently invisible to the planner — the packet exists precisely to carry decision context forward.
findings.rationale: 600 chars is very tight for a 'context packet'; either enforce the cap where the packet is authored (so authors know the budget) or raise it to a token-budgeted share of the prompt. Silent mid-packet truncation is the worst option.

findings.what_it_does: Floor applied to recheck_after for degraded waits (waits whose event source is unavailable and must fall back to polling), used at line 1676.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A degraded wait re-checks no more often than every 5 minutes, preventing tight poll loops when event wiring is broken.
findings.rationale: A floor, not a ceiling: it can only add latency to an already-degraded path, never abandon work, and it stops a broken event source from turning into a hot poll loop of planner cycles.

findings.what_it_does: Reuses the idle-backoff cap constant as the interval for re-granting a planner turn while waiting on the operator.
findings.consequence_when_hit: While operator-blocked, the planner gets a fresh turn at most every 5 minutes — but only because that happens to be the idle backoff cap.
findings.rationale: Constant reuse across unrelated policies: retuning idle poll latency would silently change operator-wait re-grant cadence (an LLM-call-frequency policy). Give this its own named constant even if the value stays 300.

findings.what_it_does: Caps planner-authored recheck_after_seconds at 7 days.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A planner that asks to sleep longer than a week is clamped to one week; the wait is re-evaluated then rather than trusting an extreme LLM-authored duration.
findings.rationale: Sanity clamp on an LLM-provided number in the safe direction: it can only shorten sleeps, never kill or abandon work. Guards against a hallucinated multi-year wait silently parking a campaign.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcodes the queue priority of stall-breaker verification-probe missions (planner items use priority=100 at _planning_cycle_enqueue.py:964 and _planning_context.py:2167).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Probes are ordered ahead of ordinary planner work in the queue by a magic relative offset that is documented nowhere.
findings.rationale: Functionally an ordering enum, not a tunable: probes must preempt the idle loop they exist to break. Would benefit from a named constant tying 50 and 100 together, but the behavior is correct and bounded.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the verification-probe mission to a single iteration cycle.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The probe tests the blocker once and settles; it cannot itself become an open-ended work item.
findings.rationale: The bound is the design: a probe is by definition a one-shot reality test. Unbounded probes would recreate the runaway-mission problem the stall-breaker exists inside of.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcodes impact_score=5 on the auto-generated 'Advance independent work while background job runs' overlap task.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Every auto-overlap task carries the same fabricated mid-scale importance, competing with planner-assessed scores on real tasks in any impact-aware ordering.
findings.rationale: A judgment call the supervisor is not positioned to make — the machinery invents a score the planner never assigned. Leave it unset/None and let consumers treat auto-generated fill-in work explicitly, or have the planner score it.

findings.what_it_does: Scans the last 32 journal entries for evidence of forward progress when validating planner feedback about filtered tasks.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Progress older than 32 entries is invisible to the check; on chatty journals genuine recent progress can be missed and on quiet ones stale progress can look fresh.
findings.rationale: Another entry-count window standing in for a time/semantic horizon; same fix as the other tail() windows — filter to the relevant typed events or use a time bound.

findings.what_it_does: Assigns a uniform hardcoded priority of 100 to every enqueued planner-authored backlog item.
findings.consequence_when_hit: All planner tasks are peers in queue order regardless of the planner's own urgency assessment; only hardcoded system items (probe=50) differ.
findings.rationale: Currently functions as a namespace baseline rather than a tunable — ordering within planner items falls to enqueue order, which mirrors plan order. Only worth changing if priority-aware scheduling is actually wanted; then the planner should author it.

findings.what_it_does: Caps manager_direct bounded intake items to one iteration cycle.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The directly-injected item runs once and settles; it cannot silently become an open-ended campaign line.
findings.rationale: Same design-intent bound as the probe: 'bounded' items are bounded by exactly this value. The item can always be re-proposed if one cycle proves insufficient.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the stored failure-reason string in each family-failure record to 300 chars.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Long failure reasons lose their tail in the durable record; distinct root causes with identical first 300 chars become indistinguishable when reviewing why a family was quarantined.
findings.rationale: Silent data drop from a diagnostic record. Cheap fix: keep a short prefix for display but store a hash or full reason for identity/forensics, or truncate at a size that preserves tracebacks (a few KB).

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded default F6 window duplicating LifeConfig.subagent_family_failure_window_hours; real value is passed in from config at _planner_orchestration.py:239-257.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If a caller ever omits the argument, this shadow default silently applies — and it can drift from the config default (a third copy exists as fallback literals in _planner_orchestration.py:243/249).
findings.rationale: Same policy number now lives in three places (config default, this function default, orchestration fallback literals). Make the parameter required so config is the single source of truth.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded default F6 streak limit duplicating LifeConfig.subagent_family_failure_streak_limit; real value passed from config.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Caller omitting the argument silently gets 3 regardless of configured value.
findings.rationale: Duplicate of a config-owned policy value; require it explicitly to eliminate drift between the three copies.

findings.what_it_does: Dedup interval for the 'Argus is waiting for you' operator heartbeat; re-reports immediately when the pending question set changes, otherwise at most hourly.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An unchanged pending-question reminder inside the hour is suppressed.
findings.rationale: Change-triggered plus hourly heartbeat is the right shape: new information is never delayed, and repetition is bounded. Value only tunes nag frequency.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds each outbound sendMessage call (per chunk of a split reply). On timeout/error _api_call returns None with only a debug log; there is no retry.
findings.consequence_when_hit: That reply chunk is silently dropped — the operator gets a partial or missing reply and nothing signals the loss (debug-level log only).
findings.rationale: A socket timeout must exist or a network stall hangs the sender thread (and, via chat_lock, blocks subsequent commands in that chat). The real smell is the missing retry/error surfacing around it, not the number: a single 10s-timeout failure discards operator-facing output. Same pattern on setMyCommands (line 137), answerCallbackQuery (line 312), and _fast_forward (line 232), where best-effort is acceptable.

findings.value: 1.0 -> *2, wait cap 30s (API-not-ok / offset-persist paths) or 60s (exception path), backoff cap 60s
findings.what_it_does: Exponential backoff between getUpdates retries when the Telegram API errors, returns not-ok, or the offset file cannot be persisted (lines 341, 353-354, 364-366, 388-389). The waits use the stop event so shutdown is immediate.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The poller sleeps up to 30-60s before retrying; inbound operator commands are delayed, never lost (offset not advanced).
findings.rationale: Without the backoff a Telegram outage or persistent disk error turns the poller into a tight retry loop hammering the API (rate-limit risk) and spamming logs. The cap keeps recovery latency bounded at about a minute. The inconsistency (30s wait cap on two paths, 60s on the exception path) is cosmetic.

findings.value: 20 updates / 30s server-side poll window / 35s socket timeout
findings.what_it_does: Each long-poll asks Telegram to hold the connection up to 30s and return at most 20 updates; the enclosing HTTP timeout of 35s (default of _api_call, line 67) is sized to exceed the 30s server window so a quiet poll is not misread as a network error.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Poll returns empty and immediately re-issues; commands batch at 20 per fetch (excess simply arrives next call). Socket timeout aborts a hung connection and the backoff path retries.
findings.rationale: Long polling needs a finite window and the socket timeout must exist or a dead connection hangs the poller thread forever. The 35 = 30 + 5 margin pairing is the load-bearing relationship; if anything, derive 35 from the poll window rather than hardcoding both.

findings.symbol: _file_content_digest full-read threshold and head/tail sample size
findings.value: 4 MiB full-hash threshold; 64 KiB head + 64 KiB tail sampling above it
findings.what_it_does: The workspace change-detection fingerprint hashes files up to 4 MiB in full; larger files are fingerprinted as size + first 64 KiB + last 64 KiB.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A >4 MiB file edited only in its middle, with unchanged length, head, and tail, produces an identical digest — the terminal-state marker does not change and downstream replanning triggers that key on it silently miss the change.
findings.rationale: This fingerprint runs across the whole workspace on supervisor ticks; unbounded hashing of multi-GB checkpoints/datasets would dominate the tick. Size+head+tail catches virtually all real research-artifact changes (appends, rewrites, regenerations), and the code deliberately keeps the marker stable through transient I/O errors. The theoretical same-size-mid-file miss is an acceptable trade the comment documents.

findings.what_it_does: After 2 consecutive engineer rounds judged as making no progress, the supervised round-loop stops the mission as stalled.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Mission ends with a stall reason instead of burning further LLM rounds; no process is killed.
findings.rationale: This is a semantic loop-stopper, not a wall-clock kill: without it a wedged engineer/reviewer pair loops forever on identical rounds, burning provider budget with no output.

findings.what_it_does: At round 12 the reviewer prompt is told to escalate an unresolvable external blocker; 0 disables it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Only a prompt change — the reviewer is nudged to escalate rather than keep iterating; work is not killed.
findings.rationale: Anti-livelock nudge with a graceful consequence (escalation, not termination) and an explicit 0-disables escape hatch. Removing it lets an externally-blocked mission consume rounds indefinitely.

findings.what_it_does: From round 24 onward, continuing the loop requires the Reviewer's explicit semantic-progress judgment; 0 disables it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The loop stops unless a model explicitly certifies real progress; not a wall-clock kill.
findings.rationale: This is the last-line infinite-LLM-burn stopper, and it delegates the actual decision to a semantic judgment rather than terminating outright — exactly the liveness-check style the design philosophy prefers.

findings.what_it_does: Number of consecutive backend (provider CLI) failures tolerated before the supervised loop gives up on the mission.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Mission stops with a backend-failure reason instead of retrying forever against a dead provider.
findings.rationale: Bounded retry against a failing provider prevents an infinite failure loop; 2 is aggressive but a real backend outage does not clear by retrying the same call, and the mission is resumable.

findings.what_it_does: Fixed sleep between the two tolerated backend-failure retries in the supervised loop.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The loop waits a flat 15s before the retry, regardless of the failure kind.
findings.rationale: A flat 15s is wrong in both directions: transient socket errors clear in <1s, while provider rate limits typically state a longer retry-after. The delay should come from the error (Retry-After header / error class), not a constant.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback for how many turns a persistent role session may accumulate before being recycled into a fresh session.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The role's conversational context is dropped and rebuilt from the context packet — accumulated in-session nuance is silently lost.
findings.rationale: 6 turns is a proxy for 'context getting big'. The real quantity is token usage, which the sibling knob already measures; turn count should be derived from measured input-token growth rather than fixed.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback token ceiling at which a persistent role session is recycled.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Session reset; the role restarts from the handoff packet, silently losing live conversational state.
findings.rationale: 120k encodes an assumed model context window. The right value depends on which model the role runs (gpt-5.5 vs others) and should be derived from the active model's advertised context length, not hardcoded.

findings.what_it_does: Doctor repair action interrupts the project's own daemon, waiting up to 15s for a graceful stop; on failure returns status failed with 'daemon did not stop within 15 seconds'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The repair action reports failure visibly; the daemon is NOT force-killed and keeps running.
findings.rationale: Fails loud and safe: no force, no data loss, precondition-checked against pid/start-time so it never hits a changed target. The bound only stops the repair flow from hanging an interactive doctor session.

findings.what_it_does: Hard idle watchdog on the front-door classification LLM call: if the backend stream is silent for 120 seconds the run is killed.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The classify call is aborted; classify_front_door biases each decision axis to its safe default, so the operator turn gets degraded routing instead of the model's judgment. No mission work is lost, but a slow-but-legitimate model turn (e.g. operator overrides ARGUS_SKILL_FRONTDOOR_CLASSIFY_EFFORT to high and the model reasons silently for >2 min) is killed.
findings.rationale: It is an idle-liveness check, not a total-duration cap, so some bound is defensible — but 120 is a role-specific magic number that contradicts the codebase's own stated discipline: planner.py:274-279 deliberately uses the provider-default hard-idle watchdog because 'the provider default is the one already used by every other role, not another Planner-specific timeout'. Either defer to the provider default like every other role, or scale it with the configured reasoning effort.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback default (env ARGUS_SKILL_MANAGER_FAST_ROUTE_MIN_CONFIDENCE) for the minimum model-reported confidence at which the cheap tool-free fast route's vertical decision is accepted (_vertical_ops.py:700).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Below 0.75 the fast decision is discarded and the Manager falls through to the grounded route — an extra, more expensive LLM call. No data loss; pure cost/latency policy.
findings.rationale: 0.75 is a judgment call about a model's self-reported calibration, which varies by model. The system already persists routing outcomes (classification_contract streaks, decision events); the acceptance threshold could be calibrated from observed fast-route/grounded-route agreement per model rather than fixed.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback default (env-overridable) for the maximum task length eligible for the tool-free fast vertical route (_vertical_ops.py:625-629).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Longer tasks silently skip the fast route and pay for the grounded classification call. No failure, just cost.
findings.rationale: A char count standing in for 'fits comfortably in a small classify prompt' should be derived from the classify model's context length together with the fixed prompt scaffolding size, not fixed at 12k.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback default (env-overridable) for the maximum fully-rendered fast-route prompt length (_vertical_ops.py:638-641).
findings.consequence_when_hit: If the assembled prompt exceeds it, the fast pass is skipped and the grounded route runs instead. Cost-only consequence.
findings.rationale: Same as the task-chars cap: it encodes model context length as a fixed constant; derive from the resolved model.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback default (env ARGUS_SKILL_MANAGER_GROUNDED_ROUTE_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS) for the maximum character length of the grounded vertical-decision prompt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: _vertical_ops.py:736 raises VerticalDecisionError ('Manager grounded-route prompt exceeds configured context cap') — the entire Manager handoff FAILS and the operator's mission is never enqueued. Same hard failure on the grounding retry at _vertical_ops.py:915.
findings.rationale: This is the worst route cap: hitting it abandons legitimate operator work outright, and the 32k-chars number is a proxy for model context that has no relationship to the actual model in use. Derive from the resolved model's context window (chars-per-token estimate) instead of a fixed fallback; a long task plus a large route-contract/snapshot block should not be a fatal condition.

findings.what_it_does: Poll interval while spinning on a non-blocking portalocker LOCK_EX acquisition; production callers pass timeout=None and wait indefinitely.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Each failed acquisition attempt waits 200 ms before retrying. No deadline is imposed by default, so no work is ever abandoned — the design explicitly avoids a lock timeout.
findings.rationale: Without the sleep the loop busy-spins a CPU core while the peer holds the lock. The unbounded-by-default wait is exactly the operator's preferred shape (liveness owned by the OS lock, no wall-clock kill); 0.2 s is a benign latency/CPU tradeoff.

findings.what_it_does: Replays the stage-decision model call exactly once when the backend returns a completely empty turn.
findings.consequence_when_hit: After the single replay, an empty output falls through to parse_stage_decision's 'manager held (default)' — the stage does not advance. The comment documents that without the retry this silently wedged current_stage forever after a DONE reviewer verdict.
findings.rationale: A one-shot replay of a non-idempotent model call on a provably-empty response is the documented fix for a real wedge, while the hard cap stops an empty-response pathology from looping LLM calls. Matches the codebase-wide 'at most one automatic retry' discipline.

findings.what_it_does: Fixed 1-second pause before the single empty-output stage-decision replay.
findings.consequence_when_hit: One second of latency on the (rare) empty-turn path.
findings.rationale: Gives a transient backend hiccup a moment to clear before the only retry is spent; removing it makes the lone retry likely to hit the identical transient. Cost is one second on an already-failed path — harmless.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the deterministic workspace snapshot handed to the routing model at the first 40 casefold-sorted top-level entries.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Entries beyond 40 are silently dropped — and project_markers is computed FROM the truncated list (lines 100-104), so in a root with >40 entries a marker like pyproject.toml or requirements.txt that sorts after position 40 becomes invisible to routing, potentially misclassifying a repository-sensitive decision as needing no grounding.
findings.rationale: Bounding the snapshot is legitimate (it feeds a prompt), but the marker scan should run over the full directory listing before truncation, and the rendered-entry budget should follow the prompt cap rather than a fixed 40.

findings.symbol: grounding prompt self-limits ('at most three targeted tool operations', '80 lines', '16,000 characters')
findings.what_it_does: Prompt-embedded instructions bounding how much evidence the Manager grounding call may gather (tool-call count, per-result lines, combined characters). Not code-enforced.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The model self-limits its inspection; a repository needing more than three reads produces a shallower brief. Nothing is killed — these are advisory numbers.
findings.rationale: Without stated bounds the read-only grounding pass can wander the repository and multiply token burn on a purely advisory artifact (the call is already fail-soft: any failure returns the task unchanged). The specific numbers are judgment calls but the bound itself prevents unbounded LLM/tool burn; if tuned, tie the character budget to the same brief cap at line 298.

findings.what_it_does: Silently truncates the Manager's repository-grounding brief before it is attached to the Engineer handoff task.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The tail of the grounding brief (which the prompt asks to end with 'recommended decomposition') is cut off with only an ellipsis; the Engineer receives partial architecture/build/test evidence with no signal anything is missing beyond the ellipsis character.
findings.rationale: The budget should relate to the Engineer prompt budget/model context, and truncation of structured evidence should prefer dropping whole trailing sections or asking the model for a shorter brief; a fixed 8k chars encodes a context-size judgment twice removed from the model that will consume it.

findings.what_it_does: Number of consecutive classification-contract failures by one model before the Manager declares a model/role capability mismatch (front_door.py:855-871 raises ManagerModelCapabilityMismatchError and publishes an operator-facing message).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The handoff stops retrying and the operator is told the configured Manager model cannot satisfy the routing contract, instead of burning further turns. Streak resets on any success and excludes transport/auth failures by design.
findings.rationale: This is a documented loop-stopper: 'one or two failures can still be an unlucky generation; three is small enough to stop an operator losing hours to a deterministic mismatch.' Removing it re-opens exactly that failure mode; the streak is per-model, persisted, and reset-on-success, so false positives are self-limiting.

findings.symbol: validator-repair acceptance_retries (also clamped at line 601, consumed one-shot at lines 905-970)
findings.what_it_does: Issuing a validator_repair authorization requires exactly one acceptance retry; the retry is durably marked consumed before use and never replayed after interruption (lines 738-760).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The repaired campaign gets one re-run of the failed acceptance validator; if the process dies mid-retry the budget is deliberately treated as spent and the operator must re-authorize.
findings.rationale: The one-shot semantic is the security/consistency invariant of the whole repair-capability design — an interrupted retry that silently replayed would let a failed validation be retried unboundedly under a single operator authorization. The number 1 is the contract, not a tuning knob.

findings.what_it_does: Only the newest 10 active standing steering directives are rendered into role prompts (lines 281, 290); older active records stay in the ledger but disappear from prompts.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The 11th-oldest standing operator steering directive is silently no longer seen by Planner/Engineer even though the operator never cleared it — standing guidance quietly stops standing.
findings.rationale: The real constraint is the prompt budget, which STEERING_MAX_CHARS already enforces; a separate fixed entry count double-caps and can drop short directives that would fit. Render under the char budget alone, or derive the entry window from it.

findings.what_it_does: Character budget for the rendered standing-steering block injected into role prompts; overflowing directives are dropped oldest-first, with the boundary one truncated with an ellipsis (lines 314-322).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older standing directives silently fall out of every role's prompt; one directive may appear cut off mid-sentence.
findings.rationale: A budget must exist (steering is injected into every role turn), but 4,000 chars is a fixed guess at what the prompt can afford; derive it from the consuming model's context budget, and surface (event/log) when active directives are being dropped so the operator can consolidate them.

findings.what_it_does: A raw operator message routed into an active continuous campaign is persisted as a backlog item with at most 1 engineer iteration cycle (iterate=False).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The mission gets exactly one execution pass plus its required independent review; further refinement must come from a new Planner-authored task rather than in-mission looping.
findings.rationale: This is a deliberate loop-stopper on undecomposed operator input: nothing has broken the work down, so open-ended iteration on it would burn cycles without a decision rule. The surrounding tags (review:required) show the invariant was tuned from an observed incident; the value 1 is the mechanism, not an arbitrary tuning.

findings.what_it_does: Each bounded-DAG mission node may run at most 3 engineer iteration cycles (1 for the manager-direct workflow) before the mission settles.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A node still failing its acceptance check after 3 cycles stops iterating; the outcome goes to review and the Planner must re-plan, rather than the engineer looping indefinitely.
findings.rationale: Per-mission iteration caps are the primary defense against infinite LLM-call burn on a stuck task, and re-planning after a bounded number of failed cycles is the designed escalation path. The 3-vs-1 split is a judgment call, but some small finite value must exist; if tuned, derive from task scope rather than deleting.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the secret-redacted model-reply excerpt stored in routing-failure errors and life.manager.intent.failed events to 300 characters.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Diagnostic snippet is truncated with an ellipsis; the full reply is not persisted with the event. Only affects debugging depth, never control flow.
findings.rationale: Unbounded model replies embedded in every failure event would bloat the durable event log and could smuggle large untrusted text into operator-facing surfaces; a short bounded excerpt after secret redaction is genuinely protective. The exact 300 is arbitrary but low-stakes.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates each operator-stated precise constraint / exclusion / ambiguity captured from the routing decision to 400 characters.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The tail of an operator constraint is silently cut, directly contradicting the function's own docstring ('must not reword a constraint: the operator's phrasing is the thing that was agreed to'). A mission can then violate the dropped part of a constraint with no trace.
findings.rationale: These are the operator's contractual requirements, not diagnostics; there are at most a handful per handoff and total size is already bounded by the operator's own message length. Silently editing an agreement is worse than carrying a long string. If any bound is kept it must fail loudly, not truncate.

findings.what_it_does: Keeps only the first 12 operator-stated constraints (and separately 12 exclusions, 12 ambiguities) from the routing decision.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Constraint #13 onward is silently discarded — an operator exclusion can vanish before the mission is even authored, with no diagnostic.
findings.rationale: Same argument as the 400-char cap: operator requirements are the one category of data the system promises to pass through verbatim. The source is a single operator message, so the list is naturally bounded; a silent drop encodes 'more than 12 requirements is implausible' as policy.

findings.what_it_does: Caps files in the cockpit live side panel: selections beyond 6 are silently dropped when parsing (lines 165, 306, 332) and a Manager rendering response naming more than 6 is rejected outright (lines 463, 487).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The Manager's 7th chosen sidebar file never reaches the operator; an over-long rendering response is discarded entirely.
findings.rationale: Purely presentational surface with a hard consumer (the Web cockpit); an unbounded manifest lets one model turn stuff arbitrary amounts of workspace content into the operator UI. Six is a defensible product bound; nothing scientific is lost since files remain in the workspace.

findings.what_it_does: Per-file byte ceiling for Manager-authored presentation files in the live view; oversize content is skipped (lines 315, 345).
findings.consequence_when_hit: An oversize presentation file is silently not rendered in the sidebar.
findings.rationale: Prevents a single model-authored file from ballooning the manifest/browser payload; the live view is display-only, so the cap cannot lose research artifacts — it only bounds a UI channel.

findings.what_it_does: draft_plan trims the model-authored preview plan to its first 8 steps before showing it to the operator for approval (line 425); the parser itself is uncapped.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Steps 9+ are silently removed from the preview the operator approves — the operator confirms a plan that is not the plan the model produced.
findings.rationale: This cap protects nothing (the plan is preview-only, never executed, and already fully generated — no token burn is saved) while actively misrepresenting the model's proposal at the exact moment the operator is asked to approve it. Show all parsed steps; if the UI wants folding, fold in the UI.

findings.what_it_does: Trims the rewrite's 'changes' and 'questions' advisory lists to 6 items each (lines 106, 139-140).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The Manager's 7th clarifying question — a thing it deliberately declined to decide for the operator — is silently discarded before the operator ever sees it.
findings.rationale: The questions list exists precisely to surface judgment calls to the operator; dropping items defeats it, and the stated motive ('show without scrolling') is a UI concern that belongs in the cockpit renderer, not in data truncation. Output is already bounded by the model's reply.

findings.what_it_does: Silently truncates the rewritten operator brief at 4,000 characters (lines 138, 174).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The operator is invited to send a draft whose tail was silently cut — the exact failure the module's own docstring guards against elsewhere ('cutting it at the first newline would hand the operator a truncated draft').
findings.rationale: The rewrite is operator-reviewed before dispatch, so there is no runaway-consumption risk the cap protects against; the model's generation limit already bounds it. If any bound is retained it must be visible (marked truncation), never silent — but simply removing it is safer than a bigger number.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the originating task text for each skill candidate in the batch placement-judge prompt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The judge classifies placement (global / vertical / stay) from a prefix of the task; context past 2,000 chars is silently invisible.
findings.rationale: Placement quality gates where a skill propagates across all future projects; the budget should follow the judge model's context rather than a fixed prefix, or at least mark the truncation in the prompt.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates each candidate skill's content to 12,000 characters before the placement judge sees it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A long skill is judged on its head; sections that would reveal it is project-specific (and should stay local) can be cut, biasing toward wrong promotion.
findings.rationale: Same as the task cap: fixed char prefixes standing in for model context, feeding a decision with cross-project blast radius.

findings.what_it_does: At most 8 project-local skill candidate files are presented to the post-mission team-learning reviewer (lines 229, 243).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Candidate #9 onward is silently absent from the evidence bundle — it can never be promoted this round, with no record that it was skipped.
findings.rationale: The real budget is the reviewer prompt size, already enforced by _MAX_CANDIDATE_CHARS; the fixed file count can exclude small candidates that would fit. Fill under the char budget (or the consuming model's context) and emit a diagnostic naming what was omitted.

findings.what_it_does: Combined character budget for candidate skill excerpts in the team-learning review prompt; each file gets the remaining budget as a prefix excerpt (lines 202, 232, 242-243).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Later candidates are truncated to whatever budget remains (possibly a useless prefix) or dropped entirely; the reviewer judges promotion on partial text without knowing it.
findings.rationale: A prompt budget must exist, but 12k chars is a fixed stand-in for the reviewer model's context length; derive it from the resolved model and prefer whole-file inclusion with explicit '(N candidates omitted)' markers over silent prefix truncation.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the canonical mission result to 2,000 characters in the prompt that decides whether the mission demonstrated a promotable procedure.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The promotion reviewer sees only the head of a long mission result; the prompt simultaneously forbids it from inspecting any other source, so evidence past 2,000 chars is unreachable by design.
findings.rationale: Since the prompt explicitly makes this excerpt 'the complete mission evidence', silently cutting it directly weakens the review it feeds; the budget should come from the reviewer model's context, with the truncation at least marked in the prompt.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the (untrusted) mission objective embedded in the team-learning review prompt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Long objectives are silently cut; the reviewer may miss constraints that distinguish 'followed explicit operator constraints' from 'durable general procedure'.
findings.rationale: Same context-budget argument as the mission-result cap; the pair of fixed numbers (2000/4000) encodes a guess about the reviewer model's affordable prompt size.

findings.value: range(2) — one initial attempt plus one repair
findings.what_it_does: The bounded-DAG planning call gets exactly one validation-driven repair attempt (with a repair prompt naming the exact validation error) before giving up.
findings.consequence_when_hit: After the second invalid output, BoundedDagPlan.error is returned and dispatch raises ManagerHandoffError ('bounded Planner could not produce an executable DAG') — the operator's handoff fails visibly and can be re-issued.
findings.rationale: One targeted repair against a specific validation error is the same one-shot retry discipline used across the codebase; further attempts against a model repeatedly failing the same schema mostly burn tokens, and the failure is loud (operator-visible), not silent abandonment.

findings.what_it_does: Number of same-thread repair turns allowed when a Planner decision is malformed (no concrete tasks, forbidden bare verdict, missing completion marker, repairable metadata errors, open-ended PROJECT_DONE).
findings.consequence_when_hit: After one failed repair the verdict is returned with error set; the supervisor treats it as a failed planning round and retries planning later on a fresh cycle. No mission work is killed.
findings.rationale: Classic loop-stopper on LLM burn: the repair resumes the same thread, so repeated failures are strongly correlated, and the outer supervisor already provides the retry-later loop. Unbounded in-thread repair would burn calls against a model that has demonstrated it cannot satisfy the format this turn.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the previous rejected Planner transcript embedded in the repair prompt (_truncate_for_repair keeps the first 8,000 chars and appends a truncation marker).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The repair model loses the TAIL of its prior output — and the decision footer being repaired sits at the end of the reply, so the truncation preferentially removes exactly the malformed footer the model is asked to correct.
findings.rationale: A bound on quoting your own prior transcript is reasonable, but it should be derived from the model's context budget, and the kept region should be the tail (or head+tail) rather than the head, since the footer is what the repair is about.

findings.what_it_does: Default rolling-session window: the persistent Planner session capsule rotates (fresh context) after 6 turns. Comment: 'Rolling-session caps rotate context; they never stop the Planner's work.'
findings.consequence_when_hit: Session context is rotated — accumulated in-thread context is dropped and rebuilt from durable state. Work continues; only continuity is affected.
findings.rationale: Two fixed proxies (turns and tokens) guard the same resource — context pressure. The token cap on line 61 is the direct measure; the turn count is a redundant guess that can rotate a cheap session early or fail to catch six enormous turns. Rotate on measured token pressure (already tracked per-result as input_tokens) instead.

findings.what_it_does: Default rolling-session input-token ceiling before the Planner session capsule rotates.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Context rotation only — never stops planning work.
findings.rationale: 120k is a hardcoded stand-in for 'most of the model's context window', which varies by model (the backend/model are both configurable right next to it). Derive from the resolved model's actual context length minus a safety margin.

findings.symbol: stderr tail in failure details (also line 501 in the repair path)
findings.what_it_does: Only the last 20 stderr lines from a failed Planner backend run are joined into the verdict's error/diagnostic text.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Earlier stderr is silently absent from the error surfaced upward; diagnosis relies on the tail containing the fatal message (which it usually does).
findings.rationale: Unbounded stderr embedded into verdict.error would flow into events, logs, and potentially prompts; the tail is where tracebacks and fatal errors live. Full output remains available in the backend's own logs — this is a bounded excerpt, not the only copy.

findings.what_it_does: After a 401 from the agent CLI, refreshes the relay credential and replays exactly once; a second 401 raises BackendLoginRequired.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The turn fails with login_required and the operator is asked to re-authenticate; no silent loop.
findings.rationale: This is the documented single owner of 401 replays, purpose-built to prevent the 'Reconnecting… n/100' 401 retry storms noted elsewhere in the codebase. One credential refresh either fixes auth or nothing will.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback host-global Copilot caps (daily premium requests, daily calls, hourly calls, concurrency); knob/env overridable. When a cap is reached acquire_copilot_permit denies with stop_kind budget_exhausted or provider_cooldown.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Every Copilot call on the host is refused until the day/hour window rolls — running missions pause on budget_exhausted.
findings.rationale: The defaults are set high enough (10k) to be effectively off while still bounding a pathological call storm; without any ceiling a looping daemon could exhaust the operator's entire Copilot premium quota overnight.

findings.what_it_does: When a Copilot error matches policy/suspension patterns, opens a host-global circuit blocking ALL Copilot calls for 24h (env/knob overridable).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Every project on the host loses its Copilot backend for a full day; campaigns pause with provider_cooldown.
findings.rationale: Policy/subscription blocks (account suspended, feature not included) do not clear by retrying, and hammering a suspended account risks escalation. A long circuit is the protective intent; the operator can clear it early via the knob. Without it every mission on the host retries into a hard provider denial forever.

findings.what_it_does: When a Copilot error matches 429/rate-limit patterns, blocks all host Copilot calls for 30 minutes.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A single 429 pauses every Copilot-backed project on the host for 30 minutes, even when the provider's actual limit clears in seconds.
findings.rationale: Rate-limit responses carry (or imply) a real retry horizon; a flat 30-minute host-wide freeze massively over-penalizes short bursts. Parse Retry-After / use escalating cooldowns starting near the provider's stated window.

findings.value: 0.75 (with 0.05s poll at line 187 and sqlite timeout 0.2 at line 277)
findings.what_it_does: Polls the Copilot CLI's usage sqlite for the just-finished call's token/premium rows, giving up after 0.75s.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Returns None (or partial rows) — the call's real cost silently never enters Argus accounting, under-counting spend against the premium budget.
findings.rationale: Usage rows land whenever the CLI flushes, which varies with load; a fixed 0.75s races that flush. Silently dropped cost data corrupts the very budget the guard enforces — wait keyed on observed DB write latency, or reconcile missed rows asynchronously instead of a sub-second fixed window.

findings.what_it_does: When attributing usage rows to a call without a start timestamp, searches rows created within a 5s-lookback/1s-pad wall-clock window.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Rows created outside the window are silently not attributed — cost accounting misses them.
findings.rationale: The fallback assumes calls last ≤5s, which is false for real LLM turns. When started_at is unknown the window should be derived from the call's own recorded duration, not a fixed 5 seconds.

findings.symbol: challenge_text[:2000] (same 2000-char cap at lines 63, 100, 119; 1000-char caps at lines 126, 158)
findings.what_it_does: Truncates structured verdict fields (plan challenge, alternative, summary, frontier report fields, regression/session-signal details) to fixed char budgets during parsing.
