findings.consequence_when_hit: Tail of the reviewer's structured field content is silently cut before it feeds plan adjudication and later prompts.
findings.rationale: These fields are re-injected into future prompts every round, so unbounded lengths would compound context growth; 1-2k chars per structured field is a defensible budget, and the primary reasoning channel (reason, 5000 chars) is larger.

findings.what_it_does: Caps each frontier-report list (e.g. open questions, evidence items) at 40 entries during verdict parsing; further items are silently dropped.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Items past the 40th never enter the parsed report; no marker records the drop.
findings.rationale: A reviewer emitting more than 40 items per list is degenerate output, and the cap defends downstream prompt budgets; the realistic loss is nil, though a truncation marker would cost one line.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the parsed verdict REASON — the human-facing justification that drives settlement, history summaries, and operator display — at 5000 chars.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A reason longer than 5000 chars is silently cut; downstream consumers (history block, operator surface) see a truncated justification.
findings.rationale: The verdict's machine-consequential parts are the named enum fields, not prose length; 5000 chars is generous for a justification and bounds a runaway reviewer from bloating every subsequent prompt.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the parsed NEXT_ACTION — the concrete work directive handed to the next engineer round — at 1500 chars with no truncation marker.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A multi-part directive is cut mid-instruction; the engineer executes an incomplete work package and the reviewer then judges the round against the full directive it thinks it issued, a silent divergence.
findings.rationale: Unlike prose fields, this string is executed: truncating it changes what work happens. Either the cut should be visible (append an omission marker so both roles can see it) or the budget should be validated at emission time with the reviewer asked to shorten — silent mid-directive truncation is the smell.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the operator-facing question extracted from the verdict at 500 chars.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An overlong operator question is cut before routing to the human.
findings.rationale: The prompt already instructs one plain-language sentence answerable in a sentence; 500 chars enforces that contract and protects the operator channel from verdict-body spillover.

findings.symbol: "commands over two minutes" durable-runner rule (POSIX at line 23, Windows variant at line 40)
findings.what_it_does: Prompt-prose policy telling the Engineer to route any command expected to exceed two minutes through Argus's durable runner instead of running it inline in the turn.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Long jobs (training runs, big builds) get registered as durable external work that survives turn and mission boundaries; short commands stay inline. Misjudging the boundary means a long job runs inside a turn where an idle watchdog or session loss could orphan it.
findings.rationale: This threshold is the front-line defense of the operator's core concern — it is precisely what keeps hours-long GPU work out of wall-clock-vulnerable inline execution. Two minutes is a judgment call, but it errs safely toward durability, and being prose it bends to context rather than hard-failing.

findings.what_it_does: Prompt-prose constraint telling the Manager to produce ordered plans of 3-8 steps (interpolated into the prompt at lines 527 and 532); not mechanically enforced.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The LLM shapes plans into that granularity band; a task naturally needing 10 fine steps gets merged, one needing 2 gets padded — soft pressure only, never a hard failure.
findings.rationale: Plan-granularity guidance prevents both degenerate one-step plans and 40-step micro-plans that explode round counts; because it is advisory prose, violating it costs nothing, so the arbitrariness is low-stakes.

findings.what_it_does: When rebuilding a mechanically invalid plan DAG, only the last 40k chars of the planner's previous output are shown back for repair.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The head of an extremely long invalid output is dropped from the repair prompt; the tail — where the executable footer lives — is preserved.
findings.rationale: Tail-keeping is the right shape here because the DAG footer is terminal, the full original already failed validation, and the repair path must bound its own prompt to avoid a second failure mode; 40k chars is a generous budget.

findings.what_it_does: Nominal cap on the previous_review_summary block injected into the reviewer prompt (applied at line 220); at 100 million chars it can never realistically trigger.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Effectively never — upstream parsing already caps verdict fields to a few thousand chars, so this guard is dead code wearing a real guard's clothes.
findings.rationale: A limit that cannot fire documents nothing and misleads readers into thinking the block is bounded here. Either remove the check or set a real budget derived from the session token limit; the current value is the purest form of a meaningless magic number.

findings.what_it_does: When the engineer's account of the round exceeds 6000 chars, the middle is replaced with an omission marker, keeping the first 4000 and last 1900 chars, before the Reviewer — the sole completion authority — judges the round.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Evidence in the middle of a long engineer summary (intermediate results, caveats, failure details) is invisible to the reviewer; the marker discloses the omission but the reviewer's only recourse is the raw event-log pointer.
findings.rationale: The primary evidence stream for the completion gate is truncated with fixed char budgets that ignore how much context headroom the reviewer session actually has. Size the account against the remaining token budget (the code already computes per-block token stats) rather than a flat 6000 chars.

findings.what_it_does: Aggregate evidence rows with ≥25% errored trials get an '[NOISY]' presentation flag in the fact dump the reviewer reads. Explicitly not a verdict; the row is still shown with its raw errored/total counts.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A label appears next to a row; no data hidden, no exit code affected, nothing blocked.
findings.rationale: This module is the codebase's own precedent for the operator's philosophy — its former hard gates (min_delta=0.02, min_benchmark_families=3) were deleted in the rewrite, leaving only this attention-directing label with raw facts alongside. A wrong 0.25 costs nothing; the reviewer sees the actual fraction either way.

findings.what_it_does: Silently truncates each stored checklist item's statement and evidence_hint to 1600 chars when loading project checklist overrides into the reviewer's stage contract.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A checklist statement longer than 1600 chars is cut mid-sentence with no ellipsis or marker — the reviewer receives a corrupted contract line and nothing flags that it happened.
findings.rationale: Bounding prompt bloat from historical rows is legitimate, but this is the silent-data-drop pattern: the cap should at minimum append a visible truncation marker, and the bound itself belongs derived from the prompt budget of the model in use rather than a bare 1600. A checklist item is policy text — corrupting it silently is worse than rejecting it loudly at write time.

findings.what_it_does: Number of trailing optimizer steps summarized for collapse-signature facts (advantage span, grad norm, entropy, KL, reward stats).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Facts and advisory signals describe only the last 8 steps; a slow multi-hundred-step decay trend is invisible, and one recovered step can clear a signal. Advisory only — never blocks.
findings.rationale: Collapse is correctly framed as a tail property, but the right tail length depends on run length and logging cadence — 8 steps of a 1200-step run is a different fraction than 8 of 20. Derive from optimizer_steps or manifest minimum_accepted_optimizer_steps (e.g. max(8, 5% of steps)) with a prompt-size ceiling.

findings.what_it_does: Below this many usable tail steps the gate refuses to label a collapse signature 'sustained' and appends insufficient_tail_for_sustained_collapse instead.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Signals are downgraded to single-step observations; the reviewer still sees the raw numbers.
findings.rationale: An anti-overclaim qualifier: it prevents the harness from asserting a trend off 1-2 noisy steps. 3 is the minimum count that can show a trend; it withholds a stronger label rather than gating any action.

findings.what_it_does: Caps how many runs get a health block in the reviewer prompt: live runs first, then most-recently-touched completed; the count of omitted runs is surfaced in the report.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older completed runs' health facts are absent from the reviewer prompt (their existence is still visible via the omitted counter).
findings.rationale: A long-lived project accumulates dozens of runs; without a cap the advisory gate floods the very prompt it feeds. Prioritizing live runs and disclosing the omission count makes the truncation honest rather than silent.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the streamed scan of reward_trace.jsonl used only to count unique task ids for the memorisation signal; when hit, the row count is reported with a '+' suffix and capped=True.
findings.consequence_when_hit: On runs with >50k rollouts the unique-id count is an undercount over a prefix; the low_task_diversity signal may mis-fire or fail to fire — but the cap is visibly marked in the facts.
findings.rationale: reward_trace files on long RL runs can reach gigabytes; unbounded scanning inside a per-round gate is a real hang/memory risk. The cap only affects an advisory label and is disclosed, and 50k rows already gives a statistically meaningful uniqueness sample.

findings.symbol: advisory surfacing heuristics (block of 10: _ADVANTAGE_SPAN_EPS=1e-6, _GRAD_NORM_EPS=1e-3, _REWARD_CEILING=0.99, _REWARD_FLOOR=0.01, _LOW_ENTROPY=0.05, _ENTROPY_DECAY_RATIO=0.5, _DIVERSITY_UNIQUE_MAX=16, _DIVERSITY_REPEAT_MIN=8, _KL_BLOWUP_RATIO=5.0, _VARIANCE_OK_FRAC=0.5; plus ceiling_hits>=2 at line 414)
findings.what_it_does: Thresholds that decide whether a named signal label (zero_advantage, reward_ceiling_saturation, low_entropy, low_task_diversity, kl_blowup_candidate, ...) is appended to the run's advisory health block in the reviewer prompt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A label string appears (or not) next to the always-printed raw numbers. kind=advisory: never blocks a round, never renders a verdict — the reviewer agent rules.
findings.rationale: This module is the already-reformed version of the pattern the operator dislikes: the thresholds were deliberately demoted from pass/fail gates to surfacing labels, with the raw facts printed alongside so a wrong threshold costs nothing but a label. Deleting them would remove the labels that map onto the collapse-diagnosis skill's signatures; making them adaptive buys little since they gate no action. The most judgment-laden pair (_DIVERSITY_UNIQUE_MAX=16 / _DIVERSITY_REPEAT_MIN=8) is the first candidate if any is revisited.

findings.what_it_does: A completed run needs at least 2 optimizer steps to be 'eligible' for the training-curve-plot requirement; shared with rl_training_health's run discovery so both RL gates agree on what counts as a run.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Runs with 0-1 steps are exempt from the structural plot gate and omitted from health reporting — degenerate/aborted launches don't generate repair-queue noise.
findings.rationale: A de-minimis filter at the smallest possible value that still means 'a curve exists to plot' (one point is not a curve). It exempts trivial runs rather than blocking real ones.

findings.what_it_does: Static diversity bound in the scale=full launch interlock: planned rollout volume / distinct tasks (or max occurrences per unique SFT example) above 8x raises curriculum_low_diversity, and check_full_run_launch REJECTS the launch.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A full-scale training launch is refused (subagent pre-launch interlock) with an actionable message; the agent must expand distinct tasks, shorten the run, or label the run smoke_only (which forfeits citing it as general-learning evidence).
findings.rationale: This is a research-quality judgment call frozen into the harness — exactly the class the module's own comment hedges ('Generous on purpose; the L2 reviewer still judges'). Whether 8x repetition is memorisation depends on task-family size, augmentation, and epoch semantics; SFT routinely runs multiple epochs legitimately. It blocks real launches, so it should be a contract-declared field the plan freezes (with 8.0 at most a default), or derived from the probe's own empirical saturation evidence, which the packet already carries. The mechanism (refuse unprobed degenerate curricula) is sound; the fixed universal ratio is the smell. The smoke_only escape hatch keeps it from being a hard wall.

findings.what_it_does: A feasibility probe must have at least 5 optimizer steps for its packet to validate (packet_probe_too_short → launch rejected); also requires ≥5 non-zero-gradient steps in supervised probes (line 700).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The full-run launch is refused until a longer probe is run — minutes of extra probe compute to protect hours of full-run compute.
findings.rationale: A minimum-evidence floor: a 1-step 'probe' is a single noisy sample and would rubber-stamp exactly the saturation failures this interlock exists to catch (a real observed failure: runs retired at step 333 after launching on drifted/saturated configs). 5 is near the smallest value at which reward/advantage tail stats mean anything; the cost of the gate is a slightly longer probe, not lost work.

findings.what_it_does: Relative tolerance for comparing the launch command's learning rate against the frozen contract's; drift beyond 0.1% → launch_lr_drift → launch rejected.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Launch refused until the plan is reconciled or the launch fixed — the intended behavior for plan↔execution drift (the motivating incident: lr=3e-5 launched against a frozen 2e-6..5e-6 plan).
findings.rationale: Effectively an exact-match check with float-representation slack (catching 3e-5 vs 5e-6 while tolerating 5.000001e-6 from formatting round-trips). It encodes 'the launch must use the frozen LR', not a tunable judgment.

findings.what_it_does: Zero-detection epsilons in the launch interlock: probe advantage span ≈ 0, zero within-group reward variance (with frac_reward_zero_std ≥ 1.0), and zero supervised gradient norms each reject a full-run launch.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Launch refused because the probe shows mathematically no learning signal on this curriculum.
findings.rationale: These detect exact degeneracy (is-this-zero within float noise), not tuned quality judgments — closer to arithmetic than policy. A probe with truly zero advantage span cannot produce gradients; blocking the full run saves hours of guaranteed-wasted GPU.

findings.what_it_does: Probe non-saturation bound: a feasibility probe whose reward mean is ≥0.99 raises probe_reward_ceiling ('curriculum already solved') and the full-run launch is rejected (smoke_only exempts).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Full-scale launch refused; agent must pick harder tasks or label the run smoke_only.
findings.rationale: The mechanism prevents the documented GPU-burn failure (reward pinned at ceiling → zero advantage → no gradient), but 0.99 silently assumes rewards normalized to [0,1] with 1.0 as 'solved'. A vertical with unnormalized or differently-scaled rewards makes this bound either vacuous or falsely blocking. Derive the ceiling from the reward schema declared in the frozen contract (or from the probe's own max attainable reward) rather than assuming the RLVR 0/1 convention.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the PowerShell subprocess that reads a Windows PID's command line during orphan-adoption verification.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The query is abandoned and returns ""; the PID cannot be verified as a teammate, so a still-running orphan is not adopted — the Curator may spawn a duplicate teammate on the same task. No work is killed.
findings.rationale: This runs inside the resident reaper tick; an unbounded PowerShell call could wedge the whole Curator loop. The failure mode (skip adoption) is conservative, and process liveness is re-checked every tick.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the `ps -p <pid> -o command=` fallback used to verify an adopted PID's command line when /proc is unavailable.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Returns False — the PID is treated as not-a-teammate and not adopted; possible duplicate spawn, but no live work is killed.
findings.rationale: Same reaper-tick protection as the PowerShell timeout; `ps` completing in under 2s is a safe OS-level assumption and the degraded path is conservative.

findings.what_it_does: Poll interval while waiting for an adopted (non-Popen) teammate process to exit, since there is no OS wait handle on POSIX for a non-child.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Just a 100ms latency granularity on detecting exit; slight busy-wake cost.
findings.rationale: A poll interval must exist for a non-child PID; 0.1s balances exit-detection latency against CPU wakeups. No judgment call encoded.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback target in-flight teammate count per campaign, used only when the pool doc has no explicit `width` (formation always writes width=0 initially, so this covers legacy pools).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A campaign without an explicit width runs at most 8 concurrent teammates; excess backlog waits. Nothing is killed.
findings.rationale: 8 encodes a machine-capacity judgment with no relation to actual CPU/GPU headroom. Derive the default from host resources (cores, GPU lease availability) or from the campaign's own task shapes; the lead can already override per-campaign via pool width.

findings.what_it_does: Cadence of the resident maintenance loop: reap exited/wedged children, adopt orphans, fold leaderboard, refill pools.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Sets control-loop latency: up to 5s to notice an exited teammate or spawn a replacement.
findings.rationale: A polling cadence must exist for a filesystem-coordinated pool; 5s is negligible against hours-long missions and keeps disk scanning cheap. Not a judgment about work quality or duration.

findings.what_it_does: Grace added on top of a task's explicit timeout_s before the reaper hard-kills the teammate's process group (`hard_deadline = started_at + timeout_s + hard_grace_s`) and fails its task. Only armed when a per-task or env timeout was explicitly set; timeouts default to off (0 = unbounded).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The teammate process group is SIGTERM/SIGKILLed and its task marked failed — real work killed by wall clock, 10 minutes after the soft time-box (a Timer that asks the runner to stop cleanly between rounds) already fired and was ignored.
findings.rationale: This is the second rung of an opt-in escalation ladder, not a default kill switch: it only fires for a task the operator explicitly time-boxed, and only after the cooperative stop failed for 10 straight minutes — i.e. a wedged process (the docstring's example: stuck in a slow scoring call). Without it, an explicitly timed-out teammate could hold a pool slot forever. The 600s figure is arbitrary but generous; deleting the mechanism would break the timeout contract entirely.

findings.what_it_does: Minimum interval between LLM strategy-distillation calls per campaign root (_maybe_distill early-returns inside the window).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The strategy.md refresh is skipped this tick; teammates keep reading the previous strategy. Just a cadence bound — nothing lost or killed.
findings.rationale: The tick runs every 5s; without this cooldown the Curator would make an LLM call per tick per campaign — exactly the infinite LLM-call burn the loop-stopper class exists to prevent. The specific 21-minute value is arbitrary and could be event-driven (new shard arrivals, like _maybe_fold's mtime guard), but the cooldown itself is load-bearing.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback for the cross-campaign ceiling on simultaneously live teammate processes (spawn_budget = max_total_in_flight - live_total, applied per tick).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Refill stops spawning; pending tasks wait in the backlog until a live teammate exits. No work is killed or dropped.
findings.rationale: Each teammate is a full in-process Argus engineer mission (LLM backend + possible GPU work); with multiple campaigns an unbounded pool is a fork/spend bomb. Env-overridable; the fallback must exist and 32 is a defensible ceiling, though deriving it from host resources would be better. It never bounds task duration, only admission.

findings.what_it_does: A claimed/running task whose board heartbeat is older than 180s AND whose owner is not a Curator-tracked live process is reset to pending (attempts+1) for re-claim. Production always uses this default — _tick_marker never passes ttl.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The task is handed to a new teammate. For genuinely dead owners this is recovery; for a live process the Curator failed to adopt (cmdline verification failed after a daemon restart), its in-progress work is silently duplicated by a second teammate in the same workdir.
findings.rationale: This is the recovery path that keeps a crashed teammate's task from wedging a campaign forever, and the live_owners check already makes it process-liveness-based rather than purely wall-clock for every tracked child. The 180s value must merely stay well above the 30s heartbeat interval (currently 6x margin); deriving it from the heartbeat constant (e.g. 6*heartbeat) instead of independently hardcoding both would remove the silent coupling.

findings.value: 2.0 s (plus wait(timeout=max(grace,5.0)) at line 517 and wait(timeout=5) post-SIGKILL at line 529)
findings.what_it_does: After SIGTERM to a teammate's process group, waits 2s before escalating to SIGKILL. Used when reaping a hard-timed-out teammate and on daemon stop() for every tracked child.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The entire process tree is SIGKILLed — any cleanup longer than 2s (flushing a result shard, board bookkeeping, closing an LLM stream) is cut off mid-write. The Curator compensates by failing the task itself, but a partially-written shard can be left behind.
findings.rationale: The TERM→KILL escalation is necessary (a wedged handler must not stall the reaper), but 2s is an arbitrary and aggressive guess for a Python process running a full LLM mission; a teammate legitimately writing its shard can lose it. Scale the grace to what the child is (e.g. tens of seconds for a mission process, seconds for a dead-on-arrival one) or make it a Curator parameter wired from the same config as teammate timeouts. The 5s post-SIGKILL waits are fine — after SIGKILL exit is imminent and they only bound the reaper's stall.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds how long daemon shutdown waits for the resident Curator thread to finish its current tick before proceeding to kill tracked children.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Teardown proceeds while a straggling tick may still be running (a benign race: the stop event is already set, so the tick is its last).
findings.rationale: Without a bound, a tick wedged in filesystem I/O would hang daemon shutdown indefinitely. Derived from tick_s rather than a bare constant, which is the right shape.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback cap on tasks in a single team formation; exceeded → RuntimeError, the formation is refused before anything is written.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The lead's formation is rejected loudly with the env knob named; no partial board is created.
findings.rationale: Bounds LLM-planned fan-out (a lead hallucinating a 10,000-task board would create 10,000 durable task files and a spawn backlog). Env-overridable, fail-loud, admission-only — never touches live task duration.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback cap on concurrently active team campaigns per project; a NEW campaign's formation is refused (RuntimeError) when the count is reached. Existing campaigns and re-forms of an existing marker are unaffected.
findings.consequence_when_hit: New campaign refused loudly, naming the active campaigns and the env knob. Combined with the nested-formation guard it stops recursive team-of-teams explosions.
findings.rationale: This is the anti-recursion loop-stopper for autonomous planners — precisely the load-bearing class. Env-overridable and fail-loud; without it a lead spawning leads could multiply campaigns without bound.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback ceiling on the width a lead may set for one campaign's pool; pool.update raises ValueError above it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The lead's width request is refused loudly (exception with the env knob named). Nothing running is affected.
findings.rationale: An admission/resource ceiling (the file's own comment: 'not a teammate work deadline'), env-overridable, fail-loud rather than silent-clamp. A lead is an LLM; an unbounded width request is exactly the runaway-fanout class this stops. The Curator's max_total_in_flight (32) is the tighter real bound anyway.

findings.what_it_does: Default priority for tasks whose spec omits one; claim_top runs lower values first, tie-broken by task_id.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Unprioritized tasks sort after any task with priority <100; pure ordering, no task is ever dropped.
findings.rationale: A neutral default rank must exist and 100 leaves headroom on both sides; it encodes ordering convention, not a limit. Only worth centralizing as a named constant (it appears in three places).

findings.what_it_does: How often a running teammate refreshes its task's heartbeat_ts on the shared board (first heartbeat also promotes claimed→running).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Board liveness granularity. If this ever exceeded the Curator's 180s reassign TTL, live tasks would be falsely reassigned — the two constants are silently coupled across files.
findings.rationale: A heartbeat cadence must exist and 30s gives 6x margin under the 180s TTL while keeping board-write contention low. The real smell is that the pair (30, 180) is hardcoded independently in two files; define one in terms of the other. Positively: the mission's own max_rounds/timeout_s default to 0 = unlimited here, which is exactly the operator's preferred shape for long GPU work.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback keep-alive command (used only when ~/.argus-skill/capabilities/gpu_keepalive.json is absent) that would restart gpu_load.py at a 0.5%/0.5% duty cycle — 40x lower than gpu_load.py's own 20%/10% defaults.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If the operator config is missing, park/release restarts a keep-alive so faint it may not defeat the scheduler's idle detection at all, silently failing the tool's entire purpose (cards reclaimed despite 'keepalive_running: true'). It also assumes gpu_load.py sits in $HOME.
findings.rationale: A fallback that contradicts the loader's own documented defaults encodes no coherent policy; at minimum align it with gpu_load.py's defaults (or refuse to park without explicit config, since a false sense of protection is worse than a loud error).

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the nvidia-smi snapshot used by status/watchdog; OSError/SubprocessError (including timeout) returns [].
findings.consequence_when_hit: Empty snapshot -> gpus_idle() is False -> the watchdog refuses to park. Degrades to inaction, never to a wrong park.
findings.rationale: A hung nvidia-smi cannot wedge the watchdog loop, and the failure direction (do nothing) is the safe one.

findings.value: <=5% util and <=2048 MiB used on every GPU
findings.what_it_does: Defines 'idle' for the watchdog's re-park decision: only when every card is under both thresholds (and no lease exists, and the keep-alive is down) does the idle clock start.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A GPU job launched OUTSIDE the lease system that idles under 5%/2GiB for the grace period gets the keep-alive re-parked on top of it (added matmul contention, not a kill). An empty snapshot returns False, so telemetry failure can never trigger a park.
findings.rationale: The lease registry, not this heuristic, is the authority protecting real jobs; the thresholds only gate a safety-net re-park whose worst misfire is mild contention with an unregistered job. Conservative-on-failure behavior is correct.

findings.what_it_does: After stopping the keep-alive, waits up to 30s for its process tree to disappear (driver VRAM cleanup lags a killed CUDA process), then reports a snapshot.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The function stops waiting and returns the current snapshot; nothing is killed. The incoming job may briefly contend for VRAM still being released by the driver.
findings.rationale: A settle bound on driver cleanup that degrades to proceeding; explicitly does not require globally-zero VRAM so other users' jobs never block it.

findings.symbol: claim/_acquire/run stop-keepalive grace: timeout=20.0 (SIGTERM poll 0.5s -> SIGKILL, in _stop_keepalive)
findings.value: 20 seconds (also lines 448, 493, and CLI default at 578)
findings.what_it_does: Grace period for the keep-alive loader tree to exit after SIGTERM before SIGKILL, when freeing cards for a real job.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Only the keep-alive loader (which observes SIGTERM within 0.1s by design and holds no state worth preserving) is SIGKILLed; real jobs are never in this tree — the matcher targets the configured keepalive token and excludes the caller and its ancestors.
findings.rationale: Kill escalation against a disposable synthetic-load process; without SIGKILL a wedged CUDA keep-alive would hold VRAM and block the incoming real job.

findings.what_it_does: Fixed settle sleep after launching the keep-alive so per-GPU workers exist before the started-pids list is reported.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Every park/release pays 2s of latency purely so the returned pid list looks complete; a slower-than-2s spawn still yields an incomplete list.
findings.rationale: Reporting-only: the pid list is best-effort discovery anyway (status re-derives it live), the lease/park correctness does not depend on it, and the fixed sleep neither guarantees completeness nor protects anything.

findings.what_it_does: TTL on the pid-less placeholder lease written at detach time, covering the window until the spawned supervisor process cold-imports argus_skill and adopts the lease with its own pid.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If the supervisor takes >120s to start (extremely loaded pod), the placeholder expires and park/watchdog could re-park the keep-alive on top of the just-launched job (contention, not a kill; watchdog additionally needs 600s of observed idleness). If a supervisor never starts, the phantom lease stops holding the cards free after 120s instead of forever.
findings.rationale: Thoroughly documented two-sided trade: unbounded would leak a phantom lease from a supervisor that never came up; the chosen bound covers a cold import with a wide margin and its miss costs contention, not lost work.

findings.what_it_does: The watchdog safety net re-parks the keep-alive only after the cards have been continuously unheld, lease-free AND idle for 600s, checking every 30s; any lease or activity resets the clock.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Cards left free by a crashed lease-holder are re-protected within ~10 minutes instead of sitting reclaimable indefinitely.
findings.rationale: Explicitly subordinate to the lease registry (never parks over an active lease), long enough to survive inter-phase gaps in real jobs, and covers the crash case nothing else covers.

findings.value: 20% utilization target, 10% VRAM hold per GPU
findings.what_it_does: Default duty cycle and VRAM footprint the keep-alive loader burns per GPU to prevent the cloud scheduler from reclaiming idle cards.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Too low and the scheduler may still reclaim cards (losing in-progress state); the docstring explicitly tells the operator to raise --util/--mem/--interval if that happens. The values only cost wasted compute, never touch real work.
findings.rationale: The right value depends on an external, unobservable scheduler policy, so it cannot be derived; it is CLI-configurable, documented as best-effort, and the default errs cheap.

findings.what_it_does: Period of the keep-alive busy/idle duty cycle; the floor prevents a degenerate hot loop.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Shapes how bursty the synthetic utilization looks to the scheduler; SIGTERM responsiveness is separately handled by 0.1s sleep slices.
findings.rationale: Operator-tunable anti-reclaim knob with a sane floor; no interaction with real workloads.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the nvidia-smi queries feeding the fail-closed GPU ownership guard's snapshot.
findings.consequence_when_hit: TimeoutExpired is not caught anywhere in this module: the baseline/check command exits with a traceback and a non-zero code. For a fail-closed guard, an errored check reads as not-ok — the safe direction — but it is indistinguishable from a real ownership violation to a naive poller.
findings.rationale: Unbounded would wedge the guard poll behind a hung nvidia-smi (silent guard death is worse than a loud crash); consider catching it to emit a distinct 'telemetry unavailable' receipt, but the bound stays.

findings.what_it_does: Caps how far up the process ancestry chain ownership attribution (cwd/executable within campaign or protected roots) will walk, alongside a visited-set cycle guard.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A GPU process more than 64 parents removed from any marker process loses attribution and, being unattributed on a training GPU, is flagged unauthorized (fail-closed). Real process trees are nowhere near 64 deep.
findings.rationale: Belt-and-suspenders bound on a /proc walk whose cycle case is already handled; the limit is far above any realistic tree depth and its failure direction matches the module's fail-closed contract.

findings.what_it_does: Grace window during which a training-GPU process that became unreadable in /proc (stale nvidia entry) is still treated as authorized, provided it was verified as campaign-owned within the window on a previous poll.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A campaign process whose /proc metadata stays unreadable past the grace (or that was never verified before going stale) is flagged unauthorized -> gpu_guard_ok=false -> exit 2, escalating a fail-closed alarm on what may be a legitimate exiting trainer.
findings.rationale: The value lives in the project policy file; the 120s constant is only the fallback, and some finite grace is required or every process-exit race between nvidia-smi and /proc reads would fire the guard. The window's length trades false alarms against how long a truly foreign process can hide behind a stale entry.

findings.what_it_does: POST image/vision API calls get at most one replay on transient HTTP errors (429/5xx) or URLError; documented as bounding duplicate non-idempotent work.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The error is raised to the caller as ApiError/ImageToolError; each attempt is also metered against the daily cap before sending.
findings.rationale: Image generation POSTs are non-idempotent and metered; more replays would duplicate spend and cap consumption. CLI-overridable via --max-retries.

findings.what_it_does: Hardcoded fallback for the atomically-metered daily Azure image-generation call cap (ARGUS_SKILL_IMAGE_DAILY_CALL_CAP overrides); every attempt is reserved in a flock'd ledger before sending.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The call raises ImageToolError naming the ledger path and the env var to raise — a loud, actionable refusal, not silent loss.
findings.rationale: This is the canonical load-bearing loop-stopper: it bounds autonomous paid-API burn, fails loudly with the override instructions in the error, and is config-first with the constant only as fallback.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds retry sleeps between API attempts, including honoring but capping server Retry-After headers.
findings.consequence_when_hit: One throttled API cannot park the caller for longer than 45s per retry (documented intent).
findings.rationale: With only 2 attempts total the worst-case added latency is bounded and small; capping Retry-After protects against a server demanding pathological waits.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds `<tool> --version` banner probes used to record lean/lake/elan facts in check results.
findings.consequence_when_hit: OSError/TimeoutExpired is caught; the version is recorded as empty string. Metadata degradation only — no compile is affected.
findings.rationale: A hung binary would otherwise stall every Lean check; the failure path is caught and cosmetic.

findings.what_it_does: Larger budget specifically for `lake env lean --version`, which resolves the Lake workspace and may switch elan toolchains; the extensive comment documents why 3s was insufficient (cold page cache) and what a silent timeout used to cost (a mis-attributed proof kernel name).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Caught and degraded to an empty version string in the recorded tool facts; the compile itself is unaffected. Note the compile's own --timeout defaults to None (unbounded), the correct choice.
findings.rationale: A model example of a documented, consequence-aware budget: it exists because the failure was observed, the margin is reasoned (cold-cache vs warm), and the degradation path is explicit.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the `full` view's stdout payload; extraction itself is never stopped and the result carries an explicit `truncated: true` flag.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Text past 200k chars is omitted from the one-shot full dump, visibly flagged; section/page views remain available for the rest.
findings.rationale: The tool's whole design is progressive reading to protect agent context; the cap is flagged rather than silent and has documented escape hatches. Deriving it from the consuming model's context would be a refinement, not a fix.

findings.what_it_does: Socket-level timeout on the arXiv PDF download; the comment is explicit that it detects a stalled transport while extraction remains unlimited.
findings.consequence_when_hit: RuntimeError raised to the caller; the fetch is retryable and cached on success. A slow-but-progressing download is not killed (socket timeout, not wall clock).
findings.rationale: Correctly targets transport stall rather than total duration; without it a dead connection hangs the tool forever.

findings.what_it_does: Sizes the deliberately-small `head` and `brief` progressive views (page-count+TOC+preview; abstract+intro lead).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Preview text past the slice is omitted from these summary views only; `section`, `page`, and `full` return the untruncated content.
findings.rationale: These constants define what 'brief' means in a tool whose contract is progressive disclosure; the full content is one command away, so nothing is lost.

findings.value: base 1.0s, factor 1.5x, cap 15.0s (further bounded by server poll_after_seconds)
findings.what_it_does: Client-side exponential backoff while waiting in the ledger queue for a grant; sleeps the smaller of its own delay and the server's poll_after guidance. The wait itself is unbounded unless the caller passes --max-wait (default None).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Polling settles at <=15s per retry; the job waits indefinitely for resources rather than being abandoned, which matches the no-arbitrary-deadline philosophy.
findings.rationale: Bounded backoff over an unbounded wait is the right shape; the 15s cap keeps grant-pickup latency low while the 1.5x growth avoids hammering the flock.

findings.what_it_does: While the wrapped command runs under `resource-ledger run`, the grant is renewed every TTL/3 via proc.wait(timeout=renew_every).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The lease is renewed with a 3x safety margin for the entire (unbounded) life of the wrapped job; renewal failure only prints a warning and never kills the job.
findings.rationale: Same load-bearing TTL/3 renewal factor as the rest of the system; the job itself has no wall-clock bound, correctly.

findings.what_it_does: Default grant TTL for ledger clients that don't specify one; heartbeat renewal keeps live grants valid, so the TTL only determines how fast a crashed owner's grant is reaped.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A dead owner's GPU grant is recycled within ~2 minutes; live owners renewing at TTL/3 are untouched.
findings.rationale: Crash-cleanup bound with the correct never-bounds-live-work design; deleting it would leak grants from crashed processes forever.

findings.what_it_does: Server-side poll guidance returned to queued acquire requests: re-poll at TTL/3, clamped between 1s and 15s.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Queued waiters re-poll (and thereby renew their queue position) at least every 15s and never faster than 1s; a queue slot cannot expire between its owner's polls.
findings.rationale: Mostly derived (TTL/3) with clamps that bound both busy-polling and admission latency after a grant frees; both failure modes without it are worse.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds each nvidia-smi/rocm-smi telemetry probe run under the ledger's flock.
findings.consequence_when_hit: TimeoutExpired is a SubprocessError, which the adapters catch: status becomes 'inaccessible' and the whole snapshot's enforcement flips to 'advisory' — grants become bookkeeping-only. Failed telemetry is never turned into capacity, a rejection, or a kill.
findings.rationale: A hung nvidia-smi (classic symptom of a wedged GPU) would otherwise block every acquire/renew on the host inside the ledger lock; the degrade-to-advisory failure path is exactly right.

findings.what_it_does: Poll interval while `subagent wait` blocks for a task to reach a terminal state.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Up to 5s of added latency in noticing completion; nothing is killed or dropped.
findings.rationale: Cheap filesystem poll; 5s is a benign trade between responsiveness and stat() churn on shared filesystems.

findings.what_it_does: Base interval between supervisor LLM health checks for supervised runs; the health-adaptive backoff doubles from this base.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Sets both the LLM-call burn rate and the minimum reaction latency to a degrading run: at most one check per 120s when unhealthy.
findings.rationale: CLI-configurable with a sane default; too-low burns supervisor tokens on healthy runs, and the adaptive doubling already stretches it when healthy. The hardcoded fallback repetition (`or 120`) in four call sites is a smell worth consolidating, but the value itself is a reasonable operator default.

findings.what_it_does: A CPU lease belonging to a task in 'starting' state with no live pid stays valid for 60s after submitted_at (covers the fork/exec window); after that it is ignored and its CPUs can be re-leased.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If a launch legitimately takes >60s to record its pid (badly loaded box), a concurrent submit can double-lease its CPUs — affinity overlap, not a kill. Without the grace, a crashed-during-fork record would leak CPUs forever.
findings.rationale: Some grace is structurally required to distinguish 'still forking' from 'died before recording a pid'; 60s is generous for a fork window and the failure mode when exceeded is mild (shared affinity), not lost work.

findings.value: 10s SIGTERM grace, then SIGKILL, then wait(5)
findings.what_it_does: Kill escalation for a whole process group: SIGTERM, wait up to 10s, SIGKILL, wait 5s — used to guarantee VRAM is actually freed when a run is terminated.
findings.consequence_when_hit: SIGKILL lands 10s after SIGTERM; a trainer flushing a checkpoint in its SIGTERM handler can be killed mid-flush and leave a corrupt checkpoint.
findings.rationale: The escalation itself is essential — without SIGKILL a wedged CUDA process holds GPU memory indefinitely and blocks all future admissions. The 10s grace is on the short side for checkpoint-on-SIGTERM trainers and would be better derived from context, but the bounded escalation must stay.

findings.what_it_does: Direct (non-supervised) run loop renews its resource lease at least 3 times per TTL.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The lease is always renewed with 2/3 of its TTL to spare; a live job can never be orphan-reaped.
findings.rationale: Safety-margin factor for the crash-recovery TTL mechanism; the 3x renewal rate is what makes the TTL reap-crashed-owners-only, never live jobs.

findings.what_it_does: Sleep between transcript polls in the parked post-early-stop discussion loop; the loop itself is deliberately unbounded (no wall-clock exit).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Engineer replies are noticed within 20s; no timeout ever abandons the discussion.
findings.rationale: The unbounded loop is the right design (no arbitrary deadline on a human/agent conversation); 20s polling of a small JSONL file is a fine cost/latency balance.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the task's recorded output tails and the rendered discussion history that seed each discussion-turn LLM prompt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The discussing supervisor loses earlier discussion turns and most of the run output; it can re-litigate or contradict points already settled above the cut, degrading the quality of the stop/resume dialogue.
findings.rationale: Prompt budget should be derived from the supervisor model's context window; a discussion whose whole point is accumulated shared understanding is the worst place for a fixed 3000-char history.

findings.what_it_does: Silently truncates every appended discussion message; the comment justifies it as keeping a JSONL line under PIPE_BUF.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An engineer's or supervisor's detailed rationale (stack traces, config diffs, the exact fix being negotiated) is silently cut at 3000 chars in the durable transcript.
findings.rationale: The stated justification does not hold: appends go to a regular file under flock, where PIPE_BUF (pipe write atomicity) is irrelevant — the lock already guarantees line integrity at any length. The cap only destroys information.

findings.what_it_does: Default cap when rendering the discussion transcript into a prompt or report.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older discussion turns silently drop out of the rendered history.
findings.rationale: Same prompt-budget concern as the callers: size to the consuming model's context, not a constant.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the shell probe that checks the experiment's launch command exists before starting the run.
findings.consequence_when_hit: On the POSIX branch TimeoutExpired is NOT caught (only the Windows branch catches SubprocessError), so it propagates into the run wrapper's broad except and the task is marked CRASHED without ever launching. `bash -lc` sources login profiles, which genuinely can exceed 5s on NFS-homed or heavily loaded boxes.
findings.rationale: A bound on the probe is needed (a hung shell would wedge every launch), but the uncaught TimeoutExpired on POSIX converts a slow login profile into an abandoned legitimate experiment — catch it and degrade to 'probe inconclusive, proceed' (mirroring the Windows branch) rather than crashing the task.

findings.symbol: single retry of a missing resumed thread
findings.what_it_does: If resuming a persisted supervisor thread returns no messages (thread evicted by the backend), re-runs the turn once on a fresh thread and merges usage.
findings.consequence_when_hit: If the fresh attempt also fails, the check is reported as supervisor_unavailable and absorbed by the failure-threshold logic; the run continues.
findings.rationale: Exactly one recovery attempt prevents both silent supervision loss and an unbounded LLM-call retry loop; failures degrade to the fail-soft unavailable path.

findings.what_it_does: Treats a bland-prefixed supervisor concern note as a 'real' concern (feeding the kill-decision path) if it is longer than 40 characters or contains signal tokens.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A verbose but empty pleasantry over 40 chars counts as a concern and can start the run-halting flow; a terse genuine warning under 40 chars without a token is discarded. The double-confirmation re-check is the actual safety net either way.
findings.rationale: An arbitrary character count encoding a semantic judgment ('is this a real concern?') that the system already answers properly by re-asking the LLM in the confirmation pass; the length heuristic adds noise, not safety.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the supervisor's concern text to 600 chars before it is recorded and shown to the engineer.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The actionable part of a concern (the exact flag/value fix, the specific metric evidence) is silently cut off in the one message whose entire purpose is telling the engineer what is wrong.
findings.rationale: Concerns are rare, small, and maximally information-dense; truncating the diagnosis that justifies killing a run is self-defeating and no downstream constraint (flock'd JSONL, task records) requires it.

findings.what_it_does: Rotates (discards) the persistent supervisor LLM thread every 12 health checks so a long run never overflows the backend's context.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The supervisor loses its whole-run observation history every 12 checks — trend judgments (loss slowly diverging, progress rate decaying) reset to a cold start at an arbitrary fixed cadence.
findings.rationale: The real constraint is token usage vs. the backend model's context length, both of which are measurable per check (usage tuples are already collected); rotate on measured token pressure, carrying forward a summary, instead of a magic check count.

findings.what_it_does: Rejects registration of a new task whose id exceeds 120 UTF-8 bytes (task ids become filenames).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A loud ValueError at submit time; no silent data loss and no running work affected.
findings.rationale: Filesystem name limits (255 bytes typical) make some cap necessary; 120 leaves headroom for suffixes, fails fast and loudly, and only constrains an identifier format.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the stdout/stderr tails written into the task record when a crashed/finished task is reconciled after the fact.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The durable post-mortem record silently loses everything before the last 3000 chars — often the actual traceback for a crash that happened early.
findings.rationale: Same pattern as the live-run tails: derive from file size/consumer context, or store an error-aware excerpt; the full files exist on disk so the record could also just point at offsets.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates run outputs, progress, and status files fed into the final LLM report prompt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The final human-facing report is generated from only the last few KB of each stream; a run that crashed early is summarized from its shutdown noise rather than the actual failure.
findings.rationale: Report fidelity is bounded by these constants; derive the budget from the report model's context length and weight toward error-bearing regions instead of blind tails.

findings.what_it_does: Discards an LLM-generated report shorter than 50 chars and falls back to the deterministic template report.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A terse-but-valid LLM report is silently replaced by the template; the fallback is informative, so nothing is lost except LLM phrasing.
findings.rationale: Guards against empty/garbage LLM output reaching the operator; the failure mode when the gate misfires is a perfectly serviceable deterministic report.

findings.what_it_does: Lease TTLs for direct and supervised jobs; renewal keeps live grants valid, so the TTL only bounds how long a crashed owner's grant lingers before orphan recovery reaps it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A grant whose owner crashed is reclaimed after at most one TTL; live jobs renew at TTL/3 and are never affected.
findings.rationale: These bound crash cleanup, not job duration (explicitly documented). The 1800s supervised TTL trades slower crash recovery for renewal resilience across long supervisor LLM calls — a deliberate, correct asymmetry.

findings.what_it_does: Fallback wait-queue poll interval when the ledger response omits its own poll_after_seconds guidance.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Queued admission retries every 5s until granted; no work is abandoned (the queue wait is unbounded, correctly).
findings.rationale: Defensive fallback for a server that should normally supply the value; 5s is harmless either way.

findings.value: x2 per healthy check, no upper cap
findings.what_it_does: Doubles the supervisor check interval every time the run looks healthy (snaps back to base when degrading).
findings.consequence_when_hit: On a multi-hour healthy run the interval doubles unboundedly (120s -> 4m -> ... -> hours between checks), so a late-run collapse, hang, or divergence can go unobserved for a very long stretch before the next check even happens.
findings.rationale: The doubling mechanism is good but needs a ceiling derived from context — e.g. a fraction of elapsed run time or expected duration — so the maximum blind window stays proportionate to how much work would be lost.

findings.what_it_does: Number of consecutive supervisor_unavailable health checks before a one-time SUPERVISION-UNAVAILABLE alert is written; the monitored run itself continues.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An alert record is emitted once; no work is killed. Below the threshold, transient LLM-backend failures are silently tolerated.
findings.rationale: Prevents alert spam from a single transient backend hiccup while still surfacing a persistent supervisor outage; the run is never harmed by this gate.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the run's stdout/stderr/progress/status files to fixed tails before building the supervisor LLM health-check prompt.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The supervisor judges run health from only the last few KB; an error signature or context above the cut is silently invisible, which can produce a wrong healthy/degraded verdict on a run whose fate the supervisor can kill.
findings.rationale: The affordable tail size is a function of the supervisor model's context window and the run's log verbosity, not a universal constant; derive it from the backend's context length (and consider progress-aware sampling instead of a raw tail).

findings.what_it_does: Caps the experiment's self-reported progress and status files in the supervisor prompt (companions to the stdout/stderr tails at lines 125-126).
findings.consequence_when_hit: A verbose progress file loses its earlier trajectory; the supervisor sees only the newest entries when judging whether the run is advancing.
findings.rationale: Same prompt-budget argument as the other supervision tails: size to the supervisor model's context, and prefer trajectory-preserving sampling (first+last) for progress files whose whole value is the trend.

findings.what_it_does: After the supervisor decides to early-stop and the STOP file is written, waits 30s for the training process to exit gracefully before _terminate_proc kills the whole process group.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The process group is SIGTERM/SIGKILLed. A cooperative trainer that honors STOP by saving a final checkpoint can be killed mid-save if the checkpoint takes over 30s (routine for large models), corrupting the very artifact the early-stop was meant to preserve.
findings.rationale: Grace should scale with observed checkpoint size/save time or at minimum watch process liveness (still writing = still saving) rather than a fixed wall-clock 30s; this is exactly the wall-clock-kills-legitimate-work pattern.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the stdout/stderr tails persisted into the terminal task record.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Everything before the last 3000 chars is silently dropped from the durable record the engineer and reporting layer later read; the root-cause traceback of a crash often scrolls past this window.
findings.rationale: Derive from file size and downstream consumer (full path is on disk anyway; the record could store an error-aware excerpt or scale with consumer context limits).

findings.what_it_does: Clamps the supervised monitoring poll interval so the resource lease is renewed at least 3 times per TTL.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Polling never sleeps past TTL/3, guaranteeing a live job's lease cannot expire and be reaped as an orphan while its owner is alive.
findings.rationale: This is a correctness margin, not a judgment call: without it the health-adaptive backoff could stretch the poll past the lease TTL and a live training job would lose its GPU grant.

findings.what_it_does: The system-wide default tail cap used by supervision, reporting, and registry when excerpting run files (reads whole file, slices the tail).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Every consumer that doesn't override it silently sees only the last 3000 chars of any file.
findings.rationale: One constant serves prompts to different models and durable records alike; the default should be derived per consumer (context length, file size) rather than baked into the utility.

findings.what_it_does: Silently clips free-text purpose, adaptation, review, and failure reasons before persisting them to domain state.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The tail of a long failure explanation is lost from the persisted record future rounds read.
findings.rationale: Bounds growth of state files rewritten every round, and the caps are generous for one-line reasons; the risk of losing diagnostic tail exists but these fields are summaries by contract.

findings.what_it_does: A manager-proposed adaptation of a data domain's stage list is rejected (ValueError) unless it has 2-10 stages.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The adaptation is refused; the domain keeps its old stage order.
findings.rationale: The lower bound (a pipeline needs >=2 stages) is structural, but 10 is an arbitrary ceiling on how the manager may decompose work; an 11-stage decomposition is not inherently invalid and the refusal second-guesses exactly the judgment the adaptation hook exists to delegate.

findings.what_it_does: Flags functions longer than 120 lines as an oversized_function finding in the self-audit report.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Advisory lint finding only; nothing blocked.
findings.rationale: A lint heuristic producing advisory findings for maintenance review; some cutoff must exist for the check to fire at all and its output gates nothing.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds EDA-tool probes (yosys, verilator, etc.); a timeout records the tool as unavailable in the audit payload.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A slow-starting licensed EDA tool is reported unavailable, and the vertical's stage guidance narrows to the tools it thinks exist.
findings.rationale: Same shape as the kernel audit: keep a bound, but license-server-backed EDA tools routinely take >20s to answer --version; the bound should be per-tool-class, not one number.

findings.what_it_does: Verbatim-overlap plagiarism gate: a contiguous run >= block_run, or aggregate overlap ratio >= 0.5 once >= 40 tokens are copied, BLOCKS the draft; shorter runs are notes. Author can tighten via novelty_budget.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The draft is rejected as near-verbatim copying and must be rewritten.
findings.rationale: The code itself labels these 'model-seed (BCC-pending)' and ships a calibration harness (evaluations/calibrate_novelty.py) that derives them from corpus false-positive rates - the calibrated values should replace the seeds. The mechanism (block wholesale copying) is load-bearing; the specific seeds are placeholders.

findings.what_it_does: After an engine-rejected state patch, asks the LLM repair_fn to fix it at most 2 times before raising with the attempt transcript.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The patch is abandoned with full diagnostics; the safety floor (engine validation) held.
findings.rationale: Classic loop-stopper on LLM-call burn: an unbounded repair loop against a model with a systematic blind spot (which the module docstring documents) would retry forever on the same defect.

findings.what_it_does: Kernel attempt passes only if geomean speedup >= 1.01 and no benchmark row regresses below 0.995x, plus correctness; result written to PERFORMANCE_RESULT.json and decides winner retention.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An attempt with, say, 0.8% geomean gain is marked passed=False and not retained as the campaign winner.
findings.rationale: The margin exists to separate real gains from timing noise, but the right margin IS the measured run-to-run variance of the benchmark on this box; deriving it from repeated baseline runs would stop both false winners on noisy benchmarks and discarded real wins on stable ones.

findings.value: 10.0s default; 30.0s for pip check and torch probes (lines 267, 288, 397, 416)
findings.what_it_does: Bounds environment-audit subprocess probes; on timeout returncode is None and the package/toolchain is reported not-present or probe_error in the readiness report.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A cold torch import (NFS home, first CUDA init) exceeding 30s silently reports torch/CUDA as absent, and the audit tells the planner the environment is not ready - misdirecting a GPU campaign on a machine that is actually fine.
findings.rationale: Probes need a bound (a hung import would hang the audit), but 30s is within the real tail of first-time torch+CUDA imports; scale the bound to the probe class (generous for framework imports, tight for --version) or retry once before declaring absence.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds tool-discovery probes (which/--version); on timeout returns None and the tool is registered as unavailable.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A tool whose version probe hangs >30s is reported absent from the registry.
findings.rationale: Version probes complete in milliseconds when healthy; without the bound one wedged binary hangs the whole registry scan. Misreporting risk is negligible at 30s.

findings.what_it_does: HTTP timeout for arXiv/DOI registry lookups; documented 'short on purpose'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The lookup is recorded as unreachable and the citation stays unverified; nothing is destroyed and the check can be rerun.
findings.rationale: A registry fetch is a small idempotent network call whose failure is recorded, not silently swallowed; without a bound a hung registry stalls the whole citation pass indefinitely.

findings.what_it_does: Rejects claimed source excerpts under 40 chars as assertions rather than quotations.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A short but genuine quotation (a one-line lemma statement) is refused as passage evidence and must go through the judgement channel instead.
findings.rationale: It defends the quote-vs-assert distinction that the evidence model depends on, and the rejected path has a legitimate alternative (judgement); losing it lets readers file their own words as source text.

findings.what_it_does: Clips claim statements, neighbour texts, and list lengths in the projected proof-graph context; documented to mark clipping and report withheld counts rather than truncate silently.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A pasted-proof-sized 'statement' is clipped with a marker; a claim citing 120 theorems lists 12 and says how many were withheld.
findings.rationale: The report-what-you-withheld design is right, but the budgets should scale with the consuming model's context rather than freezing 12 rows for all missions; a wide claim neighbourhood is sometimes exactly what the prover needs.

findings.what_it_does: Retries rmtree of a finished Lean run directory to ride out Windows sharing violations during the worker's file-handle release.
findings.consequence_when_hit: After ~1s of failures it gives up and leaks the terminal run directory (disk clutter only).
findings.rationale: Bounded OS-race handoff; unbounded retry could spin forever on a genuinely locked directory. Notably this module has NO wall-clock run timeout at all - liveness is checked via the worker's file lock - which is exactly the operator's preferred design.

findings.what_it_does: Blocks verification when more than 64 Lean source files are discovered, on the documented theory that the project is pointing at a whole checkout.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Loud blocking issue; verification refuses to run rather than silently checking the first N proofs.
findings.rationale: The failure is loud and explains itself, and the alternative it prevents (silently sampling an unknown proof set) is indistinguishable from checking nothing. A legitimate 65-file project would need the constant raised, but the comment makes the trade explicit.

findings.what_it_does: A statement-fidelity document with under 40 chars of body (after stripping headings/bullets) is treated as describing nothing.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Blocking issue: the fidelity doc must actually be written.
findings.rationale: Guards against a heading-only stub satisfying the fidelity requirement; 40 chars is below any real sentence of mathematical description so it cannot reject legitimate work.

findings.what_it_does: Declaration names of <=3 chars must appear in code formatting (not bare prose) to count as described in the fidelity doc.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A bare-prose mention of a short name like 'P' does not count; the doc must backtick it.
findings.rationale: Prevents false matches of 1-3 letter identifiers against ordinary English; cost of a miss is a formatting nudge, not lost work.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the content-digest-keyed memo of Lean verification verdicts.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Old entries evicted; the verdict is recomputed (compile re-runs).
findings.rationale: Pure memory bound on a correctness-safe cache (keyed by content digests); eviction only costs recomputation.

findings.what_it_does: Aspirational reference score (Arbor's reported dev pass-gap) surfaced in altitude facts, explicitly documented as 'a loose bar, not a target to match'.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Appears as context in prompts; no gating.
findings.rationale: An external published reference point with a comment disclaiming comparability; informative, not a gate.

findings.what_it_does: Caps a PubMed search at its first 100 PMIDs and ClinicalTrials at one 100-study page; no pagination loop exists.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Evidence beyond the first 100 hits is silently absent from the retrieval batch the dossier is built on.
findings.rationale: For a broad medical scope 100 records is an arbitrary slice of the literature; page through to the API's reported total (or a budget derived from the scope) and record how many hits exist versus how many were retrieved.

findings.what_it_does: HTTP timeout for NCBI/ClinicalTrials fetches; a timeout is classified retryable=True in a structured RetrievalFailure.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The batch records a retryable transport failure; nothing silently lost.
findings.rationale: Bounded idempotent API call with explicit, retryable failure recording - the right pattern; unbounded would hang ingestion on a stalled endpoint.

findings.what_it_does: Requires a result row proving FineWeb val_loss <= 3.28 on 8xH100 before nanogpt-speedrun completion evidence is accepted (mirrored in nanogpt_speedrun/capstone.py:39-41).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Stage completion blocked with an explicit message naming the missing evidence.
findings.rationale: These are the external benchmark's own rules (the modded-nanogpt speedrun target and reference hardware); a time claimed on different hardware or a laxer loss is not a comparable speedrun result at all.

findings.what_it_does: Window sizes for the verdict-free fact digests (recent attempts, token frequencies, training-dynamics profiles) surfaced into planner prompts; math_synth/stages.py:177-179 repeats the same family.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Older attempts drop out of the surfaced context; purely what the planner sees, no gating.
findings.rationale: These bound prompt size for advisory visibility blocks with no verdict attached; the exact values are taste but some window must exist, and 8 recent attempts is enough to spot a plateau. Cheap to tune if a campaign proves otherwise.

findings.value: model_execute_cap 4, pivot_cap 2, same_diagnostic_cap 2, reviewer_reject_cap 3, repeat_blocker_cap 3, tier_cost_fraction 0.6
findings.what_it_does: Env-tunable trigger caps (fallbacks hardcoded, comment says 'seeded from the s-cbac6ede run') that count pivots, reviewer rejections, repeated blockers, and cost fraction; fired triggers feed the mandatory tier-downgrade decision.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The campaign's ambition tier is forcibly lowered - scope of the research is permanently narrowed for the rest of the run.
findings.rationale: These encode 'how much struggle is too much' from a single historical campaign; two pivots is normal exploration in some domains. The counts should be calibrated against the distribution of successful past campaigns rather than one seed run - though having SOME downgrade path is legitimately protective against infinite model-execute ping-pong.

findings.value: len(fired) < 2 and no hard trigger => no downgrade
findings.what_it_does: Downgrade becomes mandatory when >=2 soft triggers fire or any single hard trigger fires.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Tier downgrade executes; a single soft trigger alone never downgrades.
findings.rationale: The two-of-N rule is the damper that stops one noisy signal from downgrading a healthy campaign; removing it makes the (already judgment-laden) trigger caps hair-trigger.

findings.value: min_positive_rate 0.55, min_abs_ic 0.02, n_periods 5; requires >=20 IC obs (line 109) / >=40 for subsample_stress (line 177)
findings.what_it_does: Pass/fail screen for factor IC stability: positive-rate, magnitude, and no sub-period sign reversal; insufficient observations auto-fails with an explanatory error.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The factor is labeled unstable/overfit in the analysis result consumed by the research loop.
findings.rationale: |IC| >= 0.02 and 55% positive months are the standard published bars for a usable equity factor, and the sample floors prevent statistically meaningless verdicts; all are kwargs a caller can override. Without the screen the evolutionary factor search happily promotes noise.

findings.what_it_does: Half-life fit must exceed 5 periods for the signal-persistence test to pass; permutation test uses 50 shuffles.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Fast-decaying factors fail the persistence test; permutation p-values have ~0.02 resolution.
findings.rationale: A holding-period-scale persistence floor and a bounded permutation count are the substance of the test; both overridable kwargs. 50 permutations bounds compute while giving usable resolution.

findings.what_it_does: Default walk-forward fold geometry in trading days.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Backtests run with a fixed quarter-train/fortnight-test scheme unless the caller overrides.
findings.rationale: Fold geometry should derive from the available data span and the strategy's holding period; a fixed 90/14/14 silently under-trains on short histories and under-tests on long ones.

findings.what_it_does: Lookback windows defining the canonical reversal and volatility factors.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The canonical factor set is weekly-reversal and monthly-vol flavored.
findings.rationale: 5d/20d are the literature-standard definitions of these named factors; changing them changes which factor is being claimed. Overridable kwargs for variants.

findings.value: generations 5, population 20, elite 5, mutation_rate 0.7; max_evals default None
findings.what_it_does: Default evolutionary-search shape for factor expressions; fitness is cached and max_evals (optional) caps total evaluations.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Search explores at most ~100 candidates by default and stops, regardless of whether fitness was still improving.
findings.rationale: Search breadth/depth should be driven by the campaign's evaluation budget and the observed fitness trajectory (stop on plateau, extend while improving) rather than a fixed 5x20; the plumbing (history, max_evals) already exists.

findings.what_it_does: Caps attempts to generate valid unique random/mutated expressions per fill loop.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The population stays undersized for that generation; evolution proceeds with fewer members.
findings.rationale: Without the guard, a DSL state where valid unique expressions are exhausted spins the while-loop forever; degrading to a smaller population is the correct fallback.

findings.value: topk 50, n_drop 5, open_cost 0.0005, close_cost 0.0015, min_cost 5.0, impact_cost 0.0005, limit_threshold 0.095
findings.what_it_does: Default China A-share trading frictions and qlib top-k dropout strategy parameters for backtests.
findings.consequence_when_hit: All backtests price in these frictions unless overridden.
findings.rationale: These are market facts and qlib-parity conventions (0.15% sell side ~ stamp duty, 5 RMB minimum commission, 9.5% price-limit guard), not judgment calls; removing them produces frictionless fantasy backtests that inflate every result.

findings.value: rank_ic_mean 0.015, rank_icir 0.25, positive_month_fraction 0.55, t_stat 1.5, >=2 hits + positive net spread
findings.what_it_does: Factor keep/drop/combine rule: thresholds are read from the campaign's thresholds config with these hardcoded fallbacks; a factor needs 2+ ranking hits and positive net long-short spread to survive.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The factor (or combination) is dropped from the campaign with a rationale string recorded in the trial.
findings.rationale: The primary source is config (fallbacks only), the decision is recorded with its evidence, and the bars match standard quant practice; without a fallback survivor rule an unconfigured campaign keeps every random factor.

findings.value: step_days 63, min_train_days 250, min_row_coverage 0.5, num_boost_round 1000 / early_stopping 50 (lines 53-54), holding_period_days 5 (line 177)
findings.what_it_does: Rolling-retrain cadence (quarterly), minimum one-year training window, row-coverage filter that drops days with <50% feature coverage, and LightGBM budget with early stopping.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Days below coverage are silently excluded from training; models retrain quarterly on >=1y windows; boosting stops early on plateau.
findings.rationale: 63/250 are trading-calendar conventions (quarter/year), early_stopping makes num_boost_round self-limiting, and the coverage filter guards against training on mostly-NaN cross-sections. All overridable kwargs. The silent coverage drop would be better logged, but the bound itself is protective.

findings.value: n_folds 4, purge 5, embargo 2; per-day IC needs >=10 names (line 46)
findings.what_it_does: Cross-validation config for model selection with leakage purge/embargo gaps.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Models are ranked on 4 purged folds; days with <10 stocks contribute no IC.
findings.rationale: Purge/embargo should equal the label horizon (which the caller knows) rather than fixed 5/2; fold count should scale with data span. The >=10-names floor is statistically load-bearing and fine.

findings.what_it_does: Scores candidate model families for the task (e.g. MLP viable only when rows-per-feature > 300), steering which trainer is picked.
findings.consequence_when_hit: On data-poor tasks high-capacity models are down-ranked; the campaign trains a different model family.
findings.rationale: An explicit, commented prior against fitting an MLP with fewer than a few hundred rows per feature prevents a well-known overfit failure; the scores only rank candidates, they do not forbid anything, and the reasons are surfaced.

findings.what_it_does: Floor on the prose-review score threshold; generate_academic_language_review clamps any caller-passed threshold up to 4.0 and embeds it in the advisory prompt sent to the reviewer model.
findings.consequence_when_hit: No hard harness verdict (result explicitly sets no_harness_quality_verdict=True), but the number steers the reviewer agent's advisory pass bar and callers cannot lower it below 4.0.
findings.rationale: The harness was already redesigned to emit no quality verdict and leave the call to the reviewer agent; a hardcoded 4.0/5 floor is a vestigial machine-acceptance number encoding a judgment call the reviewer owns.

findings.what_it_does: Caps the BFS over \input/\include-referenced LaTeX sources at 120 files.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Files beyond the 120th are silently never read or reviewed - no issue is filed, the review just covers a truncated manuscript.
findings.rationale: The seen-set already prevents include cycles, so the walk terminates without a cap; if kept for pathology, hitting it must be reported, not silent. Silent truncation of the review's input is the worst failure mode of a reviewer.

findings.what_it_does: Deterministic abstract-shape check: any abstract that is not exactly 5 sentences, or under 170 words, files a weak_abstract_shape / thin_abstract issue with a 0.6 penalty and a 3.5 score cap fed to the reviewer.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A perfectly good 4- or 6-sentence abstract is flagged as defective on every review iteration, pushing the reviewer/author agents to rewrite toward an arbitrary house format.
findings.rationale: Exactly-five-sentences is a pure style judgment hardcoded as a defect detector; venues differ and the reviewer agent reads the abstract anyway. This is the operator's canonical 'machine acceptance' smell.

findings.what_it_does: Character budgets that truncate the LaTeX source context packed into the reviewer-model prompt (plus limit=14000 structured digest at line 1293 and limit=12/20 span caps).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Later sections of a long paper are cut from the reviewer's context, so its advisory review is computed from a partial manuscript.
findings.rationale: A budget must exist, but it should derive from the configured reviewer model's context window and the actual manuscript size, not three frozen numbers tuned for an unknown model.

findings.what_it_does: The figure-review prompt instructs the vision model to answer keep_or_regenerate='keep' only when its own score is >= 4/5.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Figures scored 3 are regenerated even if the reviewer would otherwise keep them, burning render/LLM cycles.
findings.rationale: Hardcoding the cutoff inside the prompt second-guesses the judge it is addressing; ask for the keep/regenerate verdict and rationale directly and let the score be advisory.

findings.what_it_does: Hard-wires the idea portfolio to exactly 12 routes: selection payloads are rejected unless there are exactly 12 routes, 12 reviews, and 11 rejections (lines 429, 449, 487, 920).
