findings.consequence_when_hit: A campaign that explored 8 or 15 ideas cannot complete selection; the state machine refuses the payload and the pipeline stalls until exactly 12 exist.
findings.rationale: Portfolio width is a judgment call that should scale with campaign compute, topic breadth, and operator intent. Freezing it at 12 (policy literally named fixed_twelve) forces make-work ideas or blocks legitimate narrower explorations.

findings.symbol: MAX_WINNER_EXPLANATION_CHARS / MAX_EVIDENCE_TEXT_CHARS / MAX_RESOURCE_TEXT_CHARS / MAX_RISK_COUNT / MAX_RISK_TEXT_CHARS / MAX_REJECTION_TEXT_CHARS
findings.what_it_does: _bounded_text silently clips selection rationale, evidence, resource needs, and rejection reasons to these lengths, and the unresolved-risk list to 6 entries (lines 348-378).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Rationale and risk content beyond the cap is silently dropped from the HANDOFF that the downstream experiment campaign is built on; the 7th+ risks vanish entirely.
findings.rationale: Silently truncating the justification and risk record of a selection decision destroys exactly the information a long campaign needs later; if compactness matters, reject loudly (as MAX_HANDOFF_CHARS does) instead of clipping in silence.

findings.what_it_does: Raises ValueError if the composed compact HANDOFF.md exceeds 9000 characters (line 986), refusing to write it.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Loud failure: the selection step errors and the agent must shorten the handoff; nothing is silently lost.
findings.rationale: It enforces the deliberate compact-handoff contract and fails loudly rather than truncating; without it the 'compact' handoff regresses into an unbounded dump. The specific 9000 is arguable but the loud-failure mechanism is right.

findings.what_it_does: Caps rows read from a raw trace file in the fallback metrics path.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Later rows of a giant trace are ignored when computing fallback aggregate stats.
findings.rationale: Bounds memory/time on a fallback-only path explicitly documented as such; the primary path reads structured summaries. Unbounded parse of a multi-GB trace inside a review pass is the real risk.

findings.what_it_does: Epsilons deciding whether two conditions' reward stats are close enough to surface a 'looks indistinguishable' advisory note; comments state explicitly these are NOT pass/fail thresholds.
findings.consequence_when_hit: An advisory sentence appears in the review context; the reviewer rules.
findings.rationale: Purely advisory surfacing with the authority explicitly left to the reviewer - the pattern the operator wants. Without an epsilon the no-op detector cannot exist at all.

findings.what_it_does: A run is excluded as a throwaway probe only if its name carries a probe token AND it trained <=50 optimizer steps.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Short probe runs are excluded from method-differentiation analysis; a long run with a probe-ish name is kept (the AND is designed for that).
findings.rationale: The conjunction with the name token means a legitimate long run can never be dropped by this number; removing it would let renamed probes pollute the comparison.

findings.what_it_does: Floor on the infrastructure-review threshold, clamped up at line 83 and used as CLI default.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Same advisory-prompt steering as the other two review floors; callers cannot lower it.
findings.rationale: Third instance of the vestigial numeric acceptance floor; the reviewer agent owns the verdict.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates the LaTeX source fed to the infrastructure reviewer model.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Tail of a long manuscript is cut from the reviewer's context.
findings.rationale: Should be derived from the reviewer model's context length rather than fixed; ideally reports what was withheld.

findings.what_it_does: Floor on the layout-review threshold (clamped up via max(threshold, MIN_LAYOUT_SCORE)) relayed to the layout reviewer.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Steers the advisory layout verdict; callers cannot set a laxer bar.
findings.rationale: Same vestigial score-floor pattern as the language review: the deterministic checks (overfull boxes, blank pages) are real, but the 3.5/5 number is an arbitrary judgment call layered on an advisory review.

findings.what_it_does: Tolerance below which LaTeX overfull-hbox warnings are ignored by the layout check.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Overfulls under 5pt pass silently; over 5pt they become layout findings.
findings.rationale: Sub-5pt overfulls are visually invisible; without the tolerance every LaTeX document drowns the review in noise findings. This is a typographic fact, not a judgment call.

findings.value: pixel >= 250 counts as white; blank_pages >= 2 flags
findings.what_it_does: Near-white pixel heuristic plus a 2-page minimum before declaring the rendered PDF blank/broken.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A render whose pages are near-white is flagged as a failed render for the agent to fix.
findings.rationale: Detects a genuinely broken PDF pipeline; 250/255 whiteness and requiring two blank pages guard against flagging a legitimate sparse title page. Removing it lets an all-blank 'paper' pass rendering checks.

findings.what_it_does: Truncates handoff/context text injected into stage prompts, appending a visible '[context truncated]' marker.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Prompt context beyond 32K chars is dropped (marked, not silent).
findings.rationale: Should track the planner model's context window rather than a fixed 32K chars; the visible marker is good practice and should stay.

findings.what_it_does: Caches the nvidia-smi GPU inventory string for 60s between prompt builds.
findings.consequence_when_hit: GPU utilization info in prompts can be up to 60s stale.
findings.rationale: Prevents shelling out to nvidia-smi on every prompt construction; 60s staleness is immaterial for planning and the cache stops a hot loop from hammering the driver.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the nvidia-smi query; on timeout/OSError returns [] (no GPUs).
findings.consequence_when_hit: Prompts silently claim the box has no GPUs, so compute-stage planning may ignore the local 4xA6000 - misinformation, not a crash.
findings.rationale: A wedged nvidia-smi (dead driver) would otherwise hang every prompt build; 10s is far above its normal runtime. The real fix is wording the fallback as 'GPU query failed' rather than 'no GPUs', not removing the bound.

findings.what_it_does: Sanity check that paper/main.html contains an actual rendered paper before the paper stage completes.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Completion issue filed: 'paper/main.html does not contain a rendered paper'; the agent must fix the render.
findings.rationale: Catches an empty/stub render; 200 chars is far below any real paper so it cannot misfire on legitimate work, and without it a touch(main.html) satisfies the stage.

findings.what_it_does: Caps operator chat-message attachments; violations raise a loud ValueError naming the limit, and the limits are advertised to the UI via attachment_limits().
findings.consequence_when_hit: Upload rejected with an explicit message; nothing silent.
findings.rationale: Uploaded bytes are held in memory during validation/write, so an unbounded upload path is a self-DoS on the cockpit; the rejection is visible and the operator can place big files in the workspace directly. The specific values are taste, but some bound must exist on an in-memory upload path.

findings.what_it_does: When parking a live daemon to free its slot for another project, gives it 2 seconds to honor the stop marker before force-terminating its process tree.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The victim daemon — possibly mid-mission with a live engineer session and GPU job — is force-killed after 2s; its state is parked for later resume, but in-flight round work is lost.
findings.rationale: The replacement is operator-initiated, but 2s cannot drain a round that is mid-provider-call. The grace window should scale with what the victim is doing (idle: kill fast; mid-round: allow the round to checkpoint), or at least use the same drain machinery the upgrade path uses (defer via scheduled upgrade instead of killing).

findings.what_it_does: Operator stop endpoint: force gives the daemon 1s to honor its control marker before terminating the captured process tree; graceful stop waits up to 10s of drain.
findings.consequence_when_hit: Force: process tree killed after 1s. Graceful: stop attempt gives up after 10s and reports rc while active work may still be draining.
findings.rationale: Both windows are judgment calls about how long legitimate teardown takes. Force-stop is an explicit interrupt (1s is defensible, mirroring Codex-style interrupt), but the 10s graceful drain can abandon a drain that a busy mission genuinely needs; drain should wait on round-boundary liveness (is the daemon still making teardown progress?) rather than a flat 10 seconds.

findings.what_it_does: A namespace daemon whose health sidecar's last_event_at is older than 300s is treated as dead for web display; the file's comment states it detects a dead namespace and never limits a live mission.
findings.consequence_when_hit: UI shows the daemon as not alive / control unavailable; no process is touched.
findings.rationale: Pure display-side liveness inference over a heartbeat the daemon refreshes far more often than 5 minutes; without a staleness bound, a crashed namespaced daemon would show alive forever off its last sidecar write.

findings.what_it_does: How long a follower waits for the single-flight cache leader's scan before computing independently (TTLs 2s/5s at lines 35/37 are env-overridable; _MAX_ENTRIES=64 bounds the table).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The waiter falls back to doing its own scan — work proceeds, nothing is killed or dropped.
findings.rationale: Fail-open by design: the bound exists solely so a wedged leader cannot hang every polling client, and the fallback is the exact computation that would have run without the cache.

findings.what_it_does: If the operator's message text exactly matches a team item created within the last 90s, the Manager replays that item instead of dispatching a duplicate.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A deliberately repeated identical request inside 90s is silently deduplicated — the operator gets the existing item, not a second dispatch.
findings.rationale: Guards against double-submits and SSE-reconnect replays turning one operator request into two expensive missions; exact-text match plus a short window makes false positives (an operator genuinely wanting the same objective launched twice within 90s) vanishingly rare, and the reply says what happened.

findings.what_it_does: Builds the bounded dialogue-context block prepended to every operator message handed to the Manager LLM, silently clipping the persisted task to 600 chars and each of the last 4 turns to 300 chars.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The Manager resolves pronouns/corrections against amputated context — a long prior answer's tail (often where the actual decision lives) is silently absent, and turns older than 4 vanish entirely.
findings.rationale: These clip data fed to a model whose context window is five orders of magnitude larger. The budget should be token-based and derived from the Manager model's context length, keeping whole turns and trimming oldest-first, rather than fixed char slices that cut mid-sentence.

findings.what_it_does: LRU-evicts warm Manager ACP runner processes beyond 8, or idle over 30 minutes (never the active one).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The evicted project's next Manager turn pays a cold start (fresh ACP process, chat session reset); durable project files are untouched.
findings.rationale: Each warm runner is a live CLI subprocess; without a bound, browsing many projects accumulates unbounded resident processes. The cost of eviction is latency only.

findings.what_it_does: Bounds the cockpit workspace-browser endpoints: file-tree scan, per-directory listing, text preview, raw download, and literature scan; every clipped response carries an explicit truncated flag.
findings.consequence_when_hit: The web UI shows a partial tree / partial literature list, marked truncated; the underlying files are untouched and agents never read through this path.
findings.rationale: These protect a synchronous web server from walking a multi-hundred-GB research workspace per poll; truncation is flagged, affects display only, and the failure mode without them is the documented threadpool-starvation collapse.

findings.value: 2*1024*1024, with 0.1s select poll and 0.5s reap wait
findings.what_it_does: Streams git output for cockpit views, killing the git process once output exceeds 2MB and appending an explicit '… output truncated' marker.
findings.consequence_when_hit: A huge diff/status is clipped at 2MB in the UI with a visible marker; the kill (-9) is treated as expected.
findings.rationale: Unbounded git output (a diff touching model checkpoints) would buffer arbitrarily much into server memory per request; the clip is visible, display-only, and read-only.

findings.what_it_does: Bound on acquiring the wiki file lock; the comment is explicit that it bounds lock handoff only, never the write's work (writes are atomic and fast).
findings.consequence_when_hit: The wiki write raises visibly instead of hanging on a lock leaked by a dead process.
findings.rationale: Without it a crashed holder deadlocks every future wiki write forever; 30s is orders of magnitude above the honest hold time so it can only fire on genuine wedges.
